│                        │       ├ Title           : gnupg2: gnupg: Arbitrary file overwrite via symlink
│                        │       │                   traversal in gpgtar 
│                        │       ├ Description     : gpgtar in GnuPG before 2.5.19 can allow file overwrite via
│                        │       │                    crafted data in an archive. When extracting an untrusted
│                        │       │                   archive with --directory (aka -C) into an existing
│                        │       │                   directory containing a pre-existing symlink, gpgtar can
│                        │       │                   follow that symlink and create or overwrite a file outside
│                        │       │                    the selected extraction directory. The write is limited
│                        │       │                   by the extraction user's filesystem permissions. An
│                        │       │                   archive extracted into a fresh empty directory does not
│                        │       │                   have this risk.

│                        │       ├ Title           : libdm: lvm2: libdm: Denial of Service via uncontrolled
│                        │       │                   recursion in config parser 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in libdm. A local attacker could craft a
│                        │       │                   malicious Logical Volume Manager (LVM) metadata
│                        │       │                   configuration with deeply nested structures. This could
│                        │       │                   lead to uncontrolled recursion in the libdm configuration
│                        │       │                   file parser, exhausting the stack and causing any LVM
│                        │       │                   command reading the metadata to crash. This vulnerability
│                        │       │                   results in a Denial of Service (DoS) for affected
│                        │       │                   systems.

│                        │       ├ Description     : A directory traversal bug was discovered when unpacking
│                        │       │                   3.0 (quilt) source packages, where the packaging tarball
│                        │       │                   could contain the quilt database directory (.pc) with
│                        │       │                   attacker controlled symlinks, where that in combination
│                        │       │                   with patches that would fail to apply, could be used to
│                        │       │                   make the code used to restore the backup files to either
│                        │       │                   modify or remove the files pointed to by the attacker
│                        │       │                   controlled symlinks.

│                        │       │                   Vulnerability via SUID/SGID Bit Preservation 
│                        │       ├ Description     : fuse-overlayfs is an implementation of overlayfs in FUSE
│                        │       │                   for rootless containers. Prior to 1.17, the release-1.x C
│                        │       │                   branch preserves SUID and SGID mode bits in main.c during
│                        │       │                   open(O_TRUNC) and truncate handling on a copied-up file,
│                        │       │                   allowing a low-privileged process to leave the upper-layer
│                        │       │                    file with mode 4777. This issue is fixed in version
│                        │       │                   1.17.

│                        │       ├ Title           : gcc-toolset-15-gcc: gcc: gcc-toolset-16: gcc: Denial of
│                        │       │                   Service via use-after-free in binary heap erase_if 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in GCC. When an application calls the
│                        │       │                   erase_if function on a binary heap priority queue in
│                        │       │                   libstdc++, the library reallocates storage but fails to
│                        │       │                   update its internal entry pointer. An attacker capable of
│                        │       │                   triggering this operation can exploit this use-after-free
│                        │       │                   condition, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) via an
│                        │       │                   application crash or potential memory corruption.

│                        │       │                   search data to an application compiled with parallel mode,

│                        │       │                   Service (DoS).

│                        │       ├ Title           : gcc: Integer wrap in `std 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in the libstdc++ component of GCC. An
│                        │       │                   attacker who can provide an excessively large element
│                        │       │                   count to a boolean vector (std::vector<bool>) constructor
│                        │       │                   can trigger an integer wrap during internal memory
│                        │       │                   calculations. This issue leaves the container in an
│                        │       │                   inconsistent state, leading to out-of-bounds memory access
│                        │       │                    and resulting in an application crash or a Denial of
│                        │       │                   Service (DoS) during subsequent operations. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       ├ Title           : gcc: Stack overflow in std::bitset on libstdc++ 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in GCC libstdc++. When an application
│                        │       │                   extracts data into a bitset from a wide-character stream,
│                        │       │                   internal stack memory allocation fails to properly account
│                        │       │                    for character size and alignment. An attacker capable of
│                        │       │                   supplying crafted input to an affected application could
│                        │       │                   trigger a stack-based buffer overflow leading denial of
│                        │       │                   service (DoS). 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       ├ Title           : libstdc++: overflow leaves streambuf in inconsistent state
│                        │       │                    on I/O error. 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in libstdc++. When a byte-by-byte write
│                        │       │                   operation fails during file stream processing, the library
│                        │       │                    may still append data into the internal memory buffer. An
│                        │       │                    attacker capable of inducing repeated write failures in
│                        │       │                   an affected service can trigger a buffer overflow,
│                        │       │                   potentially resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) or
│                        │       │                   memory corruption.

│                        │       │                   of Service (DoS) by passing a string that is not
│                        │       │                   null-terminated to the std::from_chars() function in the
│                        │       │                   libstdc++ library. This issue triggers an out-of-bounds
│                        │       │                   read beyond the allocated buffer, potentially leading to
│                        │       │                   invalid data parsing or an application crash.

│                        │       │                   171ce0a552f03 
│                        │       ├ Title           : git: git: Heap corruption via integer overflow in merge
│                        │       │                   size calculations 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Affected versions of Git have a heap buffer overflow in
│                        │       │                   the three-way merge
│                        │       │                   code (xdiff), which an attacker can trigger through a
│                        │       │                   repository they
│                        │       │                   control.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   When Git merges a file, it first adds up the size of the
│                        │       │                   merged
│                        │       │                   output, allocates a buffer of that size, and then writes
│                        │       │                   the output into
│                        │       │                   it. That total was kept in a 32-bit signed integer. The
│                        │       │                   conflict-marker-size attribute, which can be set from a
│                        │       │                   committed
│                        │       │                   .gitattributes file, accepts any positive integer, and the
│                        │       │                    markers are
│                        │       │                   written several times for every conflict. A small file
│                        │       │                   with a huge marker
│                        │       │                   size and many separate conflicts can therefore push the
│                        │       │                   total past 4 GiB,
│                        │       │                   so the integer wraps to a small value and Git writes
│                        │       │                   attacker-controlled
│                        │       │                   merge output past the end of a buffer that is too small.
│                        │       │                   At minimum this
│                        │       │                   crashes Git, and because the overflow is large and its
│                        │       │                   contents are largely
│                        │       │                   attacker-controlled, worse heap corruption is possible.
│                        │       │                   Any command that does a textual three-way merge can
│                        │       │                   trigger it, such
│                        │       │                   as git-merge(1), git-rebase(1), git-cherry-pick(1), and
│                        │       │                   git-merge-tree(1). The latter is most likely a target for
│                        │       │                   Git forges,
│                        │       │                   which might use git-merge-tree(1) on the server-side to
│                        │       │                   check
│                        │       │                   mergeability. When the server reads attributes from trees
│                        │       │                   in the
│                        │       │                   repository (for example through attr.tree or
│                        │       │                   --attr-source), any
│                        │       │                   user who can push branches and request that they be merged
│                        │       │                    (for
│                        │       │                   example by opening a pull or merge request) can trigger
│                        │       │                   the overflow
│                        │       │                   without anyone else doing anything, and the data they push
│                        │       │                    is small
│                        │       │                   because the oversized output only appears during the
│                        │       │                   merge.
│                        │       │                   The problem has been patched by computing the size as
│                        │       │                   size_t and
│                        │       │                   checking every addition for overflow, so Git stops with an
│                        │       │                    error
│                        │       │                   instead of overflowing.
│                        │       │                   Servers that cannot upgrade right away can add
│                        │       │                   * conflict-marker-size=7
│                        │       │                   to each repository's info/attributes as a workaround,
│                        │       │                   which overrides
│                        │       │                   any in-tree .gitattributes, or turn off server-side
│                        │       │                   mergeability checks for
│                        │       │                   untrusted repositories.

│                        │       ├ Title           : git: Git: Arbitrary code execution via unsafe submodule
│                        │       │                   metadata during recursive clones 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Git is a fast, scalable, distributed revision control
│                        │       │                   system with an unusually rich command set that provides
│                        │       │                   both high-level operations and full access to internals.
│                        │       │                   Prior to 2.50.2, 2.51.3, 2.52.1, 2.53.1, 2.54.1, 2.55.1,
│                        │       │                   and 2.56.1, an attacker-controlled repository hosted by
│                        │       │                   the attacker rather than on a normal forge site can
│                        │       │                   exploit git clone --recurse-submodules by causing Git to
│                        │       │                   overwrite a submodule gitfile with a symbolic link. The
│                        │       │                   symbolic link can point to a directory containing
│                        │       │                   attacker-controlled Git configuration or hooks, allowing
│                        │       │                   those hooks or configuration to execute code on the
│                        │       │                   cloning user's system. The issue requires the
│                        │       │                   recursive-submodule option, and users should avoid cloning
│                        │       │                    repositories from untrusted sources. This issue is fixed
│                        │       │                   in versions 2.50.2, 2.51.3, 2.52.1, 2.53.1, 2.54.1,
│                        │       │                   2.55.1, and 2.56.1.

│                        │       ├ Title           : git: The --mirror option for git leaks secret for deleted
│                        │       │                   content, aka the "GitBleed" 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The --mirror documentation for Git through 2.35.1 does not
│                        │       │                    mention the availability of deleted content, aka the
│                        │       │                   "GitBleed" issue. This could present a security risk if
│                        │       │                   information-disclosure auditing processes rely on a clone
│                        │       │                   operation without the --mirror option. Note: This has been
│                        │       │                    disputed by multiple 3rd parties who believe this is an
│                        │       │                   intended feature of the git binary and does not pose a
│                        │       │                   security risk.

│                        │       │                   7ee792113e25f 
│                        │       ├ Title           : git: The sideband payload is passed unfiltered to the
│                        │       │                   terminal in git 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Git is a source code management tool. When cloning from a
│                        │       │                   server (or fetching, or pushing), informational or error
│                        │       │                   messages are transported from the remote Git process to
│                        │       │                   the client via the so-called "sideband channel". These
│                        │       │                   messages will be prefixed with "remote:" and printed
│                        │       │                   directly to the standard error output. Typically, this
│                        │       │                   standard error output is connected to a terminal that
│                        │       │                   understands ANSI escape sequences, which Git did not
│                        │       │                   protect against. Most modern terminals support control
│                        │       │                   sequences that can be used by a malicious actor to hide
│                        │       │                   and misrepresent information, or to mislead the user into
│                        │       │                   executing untrusted scripts. As requested on the
│                        │       │                   git-security mailing list, the patches are under
│                        │       │                   discussion on the public mailing list. Users are advised
│                        │       │                   to update as soon as possible. Users unable to upgrade
│                        │       │                   should avoid recursive clones unless they are from trusted
│                        │       │                    sources.

│                        │       ├ Title           : git-lfs: git-lfs: Arbitrary code execution via crafted
│                        │       │                   repository configuration 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Git LFS is a Git extension for versioning large files.
│                        │       │                   From 1.3.0 until 3.8.1, Git LFS does not correctly filter
│                        │       │                   the limited set of options permitted in a repository's
│                        │       │                   .lfsconfig file when option keys contain certain
│                        │       │                   additional components. Crafted keys can mimic options that
│                        │       │                    configure Git LFS to use a custom command to transfer
│                        │       │                   objects, causing Git LFS to execute an attacker-selected
│                        │       │                   command or binary while fetching objects. This issue is
│                        │       │                   fixed in version 3.8.1.

│                        │       ├ Title           : git-lfs: git-lfs: Arbitrary command execution via crafted
│                        │       │                   SSH URLs 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Git LFS is a Git extension for versioning large files.
│                        │       │                   From 0.5.0 until 3.8.1, Git LFS does not format the SSH
│                        │       │                   URL path component as a single argument when constructing
│                        │       │                   remote object-transfer or authentication commands. Shell
│                        │       │                   metacharacters in the SSH URL can therefore escape the
│                        │       │                   intended path argument and cause arbitrary command
│                        │       │                   execution when the remote Git LFS service passes received
│                        │       │                   commands to a shell without adequate sanitization. Git LFS
│                        │       │                    also incorrectly encodes default HTTPS URLs when an SSH
│                        │       │                   URL is configured and the remote host either does not
│                        │       │                   support Git LFS remote commands over SSH or supports HTTP
│                        │       │                   authentication over SSH but git-lfs-authenticate does not
│                        │       │                   return an explicit HTTP URL. This issue is fixed in
│                        │       │                   version 3.8.1.

│                        │       ├ Title           : Git LFS is a Git extension for versioning large files.
│                        │       │                   From 0.6.0 unti ... 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Git LFS is a Git extension for versioning large files.
│                        │       │                   From 0.6.0 until 3.8.1, Git LFS reads Git configuration
│                        │       │                   options defined for a submodule without checking certain
│                        │       │                   values for embedded line-ending control characters. A
│                        │       │                   malicious repository can insert control characters such as
│                        │       │                    line feed (LF) into those values to mimic options that
│                        │       │                   cause Git LFS to execute an attacker-controlled command or
│                        │       │                    binary while fetching or adding objects. This issue is
│                        │       │                   fixed in version 3.8.1.

│                        │       ├ Title           : git-lfs: Git LFS: Information disclosure via unintended
│                        │       │                   cookie forwarding during HTTP redirects 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Git LFS is a Git extension for versioning large files.
│                        │       │                   From 0.5.0 until 3.8.1, Git LFS may forward a Cookie
│                        │       │                   header after an HTTP redirect to a host other than the one
│                        │       │                    for which the header was intended. That unintended host
│                        │       │                   can therefore receive cookies containing credentials or
│                        │       │                   other confidential values. Authorization headers are never
│                        │       │                    forwarded to inappropriate hosts and are not the affected
│                        │       │                    secret in this vulnerability. This issue is fixed in
│                        │       │                   version 3.8.1.

│                        │       │                   7653ecfac27c7 
│                        │       ├ Title           : git: git: Heap corruption via integer overflow in merge
│                        │       │                   size calculations 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Affected versions of Git have a heap buffer overflow in
│                        │       │                   the three-way merge
│                        │       │                   code (xdiff), which an attacker can trigger through a
│                        │       │                   repository they
│                        │       │                   control.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   When Git merges a file, it first adds up the size of the
│                        │       │                   merged
│                        │       │                   output, allocates a buffer of that size, and then writes
│                        │       │                   the output into
│                        │       │                   it. That total was kept in a 32-bit signed integer. The
│                        │       │                   conflict-marker-size attribute, which can be set from a
│                        │       │                   committed
│                        │       │                   .gitattributes file, accepts any positive integer, and the
│                        │       │                    markers are
│                        │       │                   written several times for every conflict. A small file
│                        │       │                   with a huge marker
│                        │       │                   size and many separate conflicts can therefore push the
│                        │       │                   total past 4 GiB,
│                        │       │                   so the integer wraps to a small value and Git writes
│                        │       │                   attacker-controlled
│                        │       │                   merge output past the end of a buffer that is too small.
│                        │       │                   At minimum this
│                        │       │                   crashes Git, and because the overflow is large and its
│                        │       │                   contents are largely
│                        │       │                   attacker-controlled, worse heap corruption is possible.
│                        │       │                   Any command that does a textual three-way merge can
│                        │       │                   trigger it, such
│                        │       │                   as git-merge(1), git-rebase(1), git-cherry-pick(1), and
│                        │       │                   git-merge-tree(1). The latter is most likely a target for
│                        │       │                   Git forges,
│                        │       │                   which might use git-merge-tree(1) on the server-side to
│                        │       │                   check
│                        │       │                   mergeability. When the server reads attributes from trees
│                        │       │                   in the
│                        │       │                   repository (for example through attr.tree or
│                        │       │                   --attr-source), any
│                        │       │                   user who can push branches and request that they be merged
│                        │       │                    (for
│                        │       │                   example by opening a pull or merge request) can trigger
│                        │       │                   the overflow
│                        │       │                   without anyone else doing anything, and the data they push
│                        │       │                    is small
│                        │       │                   because the oversized output only appears during the
│                        │       │                   merge.
│                        │       │                   The problem has been patched by computing the size as
│                        │       │                   size_t and
│                        │       │                   checking every addition for overflow, so Git stops with an
│                        │       │                    error
│                        │       │                   instead of overflowing.
│                        │       │                   Servers that cannot upgrade right away can add
│                        │       │                   * conflict-marker-size=7
│                        │       │                   to each repository's info/attributes as a workaround,
│                        │       │                   which overrides
│                        │       │                   any in-tree .gitattributes, or turn off server-side
│                        │       │                   mergeability checks for
│                        │       │                   untrusted repositories.

│                        │       ├ Title           : git: Git: Arbitrary code execution via unsafe submodule
│                        │       │                   metadata during recursive clones 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Git is a fast, scalable, distributed revision control
│                        │       │                   system with an unusually rich command set that provides
│                        │       │                   both high-level operations and full access to internals.
│                        │       │                   Prior to 2.50.2, 2.51.3, 2.52.1, 2.53.1, 2.54.1, 2.55.1,
│                        │       │                   and 2.56.1, an attacker-controlled repository hosted by
│                        │       │                   the attacker rather than on a normal forge site can
│                        │       │                   exploit git clone --recurse-submodules by causing Git to
│                        │       │                   overwrite a submodule gitfile with a symbolic link. The
│                        │       │                   symbolic link can point to a directory containing
│                        │       │                   attacker-controlled Git configuration or hooks, allowing
│                        │       │                   those hooks or configuration to execute code on the
│                        │       │                   cloning user's system. The issue requires the
│                        │       │                   recursive-submodule option, and users should avoid cloning
│                        │       │                    repositories from untrusted sources. This issue is fixed
│                        │       │                   in versions 2.50.2, 2.51.3, 2.52.1, 2.53.1, 2.54.1,
│                        │       │                   2.55.1, and 2.56.1.

│                        │       ├ Title           : git: The --mirror option for git leaks secret for deleted
│                        │       │                   content, aka the "GitBleed" 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The --mirror documentation for Git through 2.35.1 does not
│                        │       │                    mention the availability of deleted content, aka the
│                        │       │                   "GitBleed" issue. This could present a security risk if
│                        │       │                   information-disclosure auditing processes rely on a clone

│                        │       │                    disputed by multiple 3rd parties who believe this is an
│                        │       │                   intended feature of the git binary and does not pose a
│                        │       │                   security risk.

│                        │       │                   e03c874bcbf27 
│                        │       ├ Title           : git: The sideband payload is passed unfiltered to the
│                        │       │                   terminal in git 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Git is a source code management tool. When cloning from a
│                        │       │                   server (or fetching, or pushing), informational or error
│                        │       │                   messages are transported from the remote Git process to
│                        │       │                   the client via the so-called "sideband channel". These
│                        │       │                   messages will be prefixed with "remote:" and printed
│                        │       │                   directly to the standard error output. Typically, this
│                        │       │                   standard error output is connected to a terminal that
│                        │       │                   understands ANSI escape sequences, which Git did not
│                        │       │                   protect against. Most modern terminals support control
│                        │       │                   sequences that can be used by a malicious actor to hide
│                        │       │                   and misrepresent information, or to mislead the user into
│                        │       │                   executing untrusted scripts. As requested on the
│                        │       │                   git-security mailing list, the patches are under
│                        │       │                   discussion on the public mailing list. Users are advised
│                        │       │                   to update as soon as possible. Users unable to upgrade
│                        │       │                   should avoid recursive clones unless they are from trusted
│                        │       │                    sources.

│                        │       │                   935d061782229 
│                        │       ├ Title           : gnupg: GnuPG: Signature bypass via form feed character in
│                        │       │                   signed messages 
│                        │       ├ Description     : In GnuPG through 2.4.8, if a signed message has \f at the
│                        │       │                   end of a plaintext line, an adversary can construct a
│                        │       │                   modified message that places additional text after the
│                        │       │                   signed material, such that signature verification of the
│                        │       │                   modified message succeeds (although an "invalid armor"
│                        │       │                   message is printed during verification). This is related
│                        │       │                   to use of \f as a marker to denote truncation of a long
│                        │       │                   plaintext line.

│                        │       ├ Title           : gnupg2: gnupg: Arbitrary file overwrite via symlink
│                        │       │                   traversal in gpgtar 
│                        │       ├ Description     : gpgtar in GnuPG before 2.5.19 can allow file overwrite via
│                        │       │                    crafted data in an archive. When extracting an untrusted
│                        │       │                   archive with --directory (aka -C) into an existing
│                        │       │                   directory containing a pre-existing symlink, gpgtar can
│                        │       │                   follow that symlink and create or overwrite a file outside
│                        │       │                    the selected extraction directory. The write is limited
│                        │       │                   by the extraction user's filesystem permissions. An
│                        │       │                   archive extracted into a fresh empty directory does not
│                        │       │                   have this risk.

│                        │       │                   18805e4c2a3a0 
│                        │       ├ Title           : gnupg: GnuPG: Signature bypass via form feed character in
│                        │       │                   signed messages 
│                        │       ├ Description     : In GnuPG through 2.4.8, if a signed message has \f at the
│                        │       │                   end of a plaintext line, an adversary can construct a
│                        │       │                   modified message that places additional text after the
│                        │       │                   signed material, such that signature verification of the
│                        │       │                   modified message succeeds (although an "invalid armor"
│                        │       │                   message is printed during verification). This is related
│                        │       │                   to use of \f as a marker to denote truncation of a long
│                        │       │                   plaintext line.

│                        │       ├ Title           : gnupg2: gnupg: Arbitrary file overwrite via symlink
│                        │       │                   traversal in gpgtar 
│                        │       ├ Description     : gpgtar in GnuPG before 2.5.19 can allow file overwrite via
│                        │       │                    crafted data in an archive. When extracting an untrusted
│                        │       │                   archive with --directory (aka -C) into an existing
│                        │       │                   directory containing a pre-existing symlink, gpgtar can
│                        │       │                   follow that symlink and create or overwrite a file outside
│                        │       │                    the selected extraction directory. The write is limited
│                        │       │                   by the extraction user's filesystem permissions. An
│                        │       │                   archive extracted into a fresh empty directory does not
│                        │       │                   have this risk.

│                        │       │                   signed messages 
│                        │       ├ Description     : In GnuPG through 2.4.8, if a signed message has \f at the
│                        │       │                   end of a plaintext line, an adversary can construct a
│                        │       │                   modified message that places additional text after the
│                        │       │                   signed material, such that signature verification of the
│                        │       │                   modified message succeeds (although an "invalid armor"
│                        │       │                   message is printed during verification). This is related
│                        │       │                   to use of \f as a marker to denote truncation of a long
│                        │       │                   plaintext line.

│                        │       │                   211dcebd157d0 
│                        │       ├ Title           : gnupg2: gnupg: Arbitrary file overwrite via symlink
│                        │       │                   traversal in gpgtar 
│                        │       ├ Description     : gpgtar in GnuPG before 2.5.19 can allow file overwrite via
│                        │       │                    crafted data in an archive. When extracting an untrusted
│                        │       │                   archive with --directory (aka -C) into an existing
│                        │       │                   directory containing a pre-existing symlink, gpgtar can
│                        │       │                   follow that symlink and create or overwrite a file outside
│                        │       │                    the selected extraction directory. The write is limited
│                        │       │                   by the extraction user's filesystem permissions. An
│                        │       │                   archive extracted into a fresh empty directory does not
│                        │       │                   have this risk.

│                        │       ├ Title           : podman: containers-common: containers-common: default
│                        │       │                   seccomp AF_VSOCK/NETLINK_AUDIT deny rules bypassable via
│                        │       │                   32-bit truncation 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in the default seccomp profile used by
│                        │       │                   Podman via containers-common. Deny rules for AF_VSOCK and
│                        │       │                   NETLINK_AUDIT compared socket arguments with unmasked
│                        │       │                   64-bit equality. Because the kernel truncates those int
│                        │       │                   arguments to 32 bits, setting upper bits can bypass the
│                        │       │                   deny rules.

│                        │       │                   706f91e877074 
│                        │       ├ Title           : gnupg: GnuPG: Signature bypass via form feed character in
│                        │       │                   signed messages 
│                        │       ├ Description     : In GnuPG through 2.4.8, if a signed message has \f at the
│                        │       │                   end of a plaintext line, an adversary can construct a
│                        │       │                   modified message that places additional text after the
│                        │       │                   signed material, such that signature verification of the
│                        │       │                   modified message succeeds (although an "invalid armor"
│                        │       │                   message is printed during verification). This is related
│                        │       │                   to use of \f as a marker to denote truncation of a long
│                        │       │                   plaintext line.

│                        │       ├ Title           : gnupg2: gnupg: Arbitrary file overwrite via symlink
│                        │       │                   traversal in gpgtar 
│                        │       ├ Description     : gpgtar in GnuPG before 2.5.19 can allow file overwrite via
│                        │       │                    crafted data in an archive. When extracting an untrusted
│                        │       │                   archive with --directory (aka -C) into an existing
│                        │       │                   directory containing a pre-existing symlink, gpgtar can
│                        │       │                   follow that symlink and create or overwrite a file outside
│                        │       │                    the selected extraction directory. The write is limited
│                        │       │                   by the extraction user's filesystem permissions. An
│                        │       │                   archive extracted into a fresh empty directory does not
│                        │       │                   have this risk.

│                        │       │                   1800c9fd8a10a 
│                        │       ├ Title           : gnupg: GnuPG: Signature bypass via form feed character in
│                        │       │                   signed messages 
│                        │       ├ Description     : In GnuPG through 2.4.8, if a signed message has \f at the
│                        │       │                   end of a plaintext line, an adversary can construct a
│                        │       │                   modified message that places additional text after the
│                        │       │                   signed material, such that signature verification of the
│                        │       │                   modified message succeeds (although an "invalid armor"
│                        │       │                   message is printed during verification). This is related
│                        │       │                   to use of \f as a marker to denote truncation of a long
│                        │       │                   plaintext line.

│                        │       ├ Title           : gnupg2: gnupg: Arbitrary file overwrite via symlink
│                        │       │                   traversal in gpgtar 
│                        │       ├ Description     : gpgtar in GnuPG before 2.5.19 can allow file overwrite via
│                        │       │                    crafted data in an archive. When extracting an untrusted
│                        │       │                   archive with --directory (aka -C) into an existing
│                        │       │                   directory containing a pre-existing symlink, gpgtar can
│                        │       │                   follow that symlink and create or overwrite a file outside
│                        │       │                    the selected extraction directory. The write is limited
│                        │       │                   by the extraction user's filesystem permissions. An
│                        │       │                   archive extracted into a fresh empty directory does not
│                        │       │                   have this risk.

│                        │       │                   98fcc2fda9e40 
│                        │       ├ Title           : gnupg: GnuPG: Signature bypass via form feed character in
│                        │       │                   signed messages 
│                        │       ├ Description     : In GnuPG through 2.4.8, if a signed message has \f at the
│                        │       │                   end of a plaintext line, an adversary can construct a
│                        │       │                   modified message that places additional text after the
│                        │       │                   signed material, such that signature verification of the
│                        │       │                   modified message succeeds (although an "invalid armor"
│                        │       │                   message is printed during verification). This is related
│                        │       │                   to use of \f as a marker to denote truncation of a long
│                        │       │                   plaintext line.

│                        │       │                   39ffc61977f90 
│                        │       ├ Title           : gnupg2: gnupg: Arbitrary file overwrite via symlink
│                        │       │                   traversal in gpgtar 
│                        │       ├ Description     : gpgtar in GnuPG before 2.5.19 can allow file overwrite via
│                        │       │                    crafted data in an archive. When extracting an untrusted
│                        │       │                   archive with --directory (aka -C) into an existing
│                        │       │                   directory containing a pre-existing symlink, gpgtar can
│                        │       │                   follow that symlink and create or overwrite a file outside
│                        │       │                    the selected extraction directory. The write is limited
│                        │       │                   by the extraction user's filesystem permissions. An
│                        │       │                   archive extracted into a fresh empty directory does not
│                        │       │                   have this risk.

│                        │       │                   8ac4518d59466 
│                        │       ├ Title           : gnupg: GnuPG: Signature bypass via form feed character in
│                        │       │                   signed messages 
│                        │       ├ Description     : In GnuPG through 2.4.8, if a signed message has \f at the
│                        │       │                   end of a plaintext line, an adversary can construct a
│                        │       │                   modified message that places additional text after the
│                        │       │                   signed material, such that signature verification of the
│                        │       │                   modified message succeeds (although an "invalid armor"
│                        │       │                   message is printed during verification). This is related
│                        │       │                   to use of \f as a marker to denote truncation of a long
│                        │       │                   plaintext line.

│                        │       │                   3ccd271fd6133 
│                        │       ├ Title           : gnupg2: gnupg: Arbitrary file overwrite via symlink
│                        │       │                   traversal in gpgtar 
│                        │       ├ Description     : gpgtar in GnuPG before 2.5.19 can allow file overwrite via
│                        │       │                    crafted data in an archive. When extracting an untrusted
│                        │       │                   archive with --directory (aka -C) into an existing
│                        │       │                   directory containing a pre-existing symlink, gpgtar can
│                        │       │                   follow that symlink and create or overwrite a file outside
│                        │       │                    the selected extraction directory. The write is limited
│                        │       │                   by the extraction user's filesystem permissions. An
│                        │       │                   archive extracted into a fresh empty directory does not
│                        │       │                   have this risk.

│                        │       │                   traversal in gpgtar 
│                        │       ├ Description     : gpgtar in GnuPG before 2.5.19 can allow file overwrite via
│                        │       │                    crafted data in an archive. When extracting an untrusted
│                        │       │                   archive with --directory (aka -C) into an existing
│                        │       │                   directory containing a pre-existing symlink, gpgtar can
│                        │       │                   follow that symlink and create or overwrite a file outside
│                        │       │                    the selected extraction directory. The write is limited
│                        │       │                   by the extraction user's filesystem permissions. An
│                        │       │                   archive extracted into a fresh empty directory does not
│                        │       │                   have this risk.

│                        │       ├ Title           : gnupg: GnuPG: Signature bypass via form feed character in
│                        │       │                   signed messages 
│                        │       ├ Description     : In GnuPG through 2.4.8, if a signed message has \f at the
│                        │       │                   end of a plaintext line, an adversary can construct a
│                        │       │                   modified message that places additional text after the
│                        │       │                   signed material, such that signature verification of the
│                        │       │                   modified message succeeds (although an "invalid armor"
│                        │       │                   message is printed during verification). This is related
│                        │       │                   to use of \f as a marker to denote truncation of a long
│                        │       │                   plaintext line.

│                        │       ├ Title           : gnupg2: gnupg: Arbitrary file overwrite via symlink
│                        │       │                   traversal in gpgtar 
│                        │       ├ Description     : gpgtar in GnuPG before 2.5.19 can allow file overwrite via
│                        │       │                    crafted data in an archive. When extracting an untrusted
│                        │       │                   archive with --directory (aka -C) into an existing
│                        │       │                   directory containing a pre-existing symlink, gpgtar can
│                        │       │                   follow that symlink and create or overwrite a file outside
│                        │       │                    the selected extraction directory. The write is limited
│                        │       │                   by the extraction user's filesystem permissions. An
│                        │       │                   archive extracted into a fresh empty directory does not
│                        │       │                   have this risk.

│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: krb5: Denial of Service via malformed PAC in
│                        │       │                   S4U2Proxy requests 
│                        │       ├ Description     : MIT krb5 through 1.22.2 contains a NULL pointer
│                        │       │                   dereference vulnerability in the KDC's
│                        │       │                   get_pac_princ_with_realm() that returns success while
│                        │       │                   leaving the client principal NULL on malformed names. A
│                        │       │                   malicious or compromised cross-realm trusted KDC can send
│                        │       │                   an S4U2Proxy request with a PAC carrying a malformed
│                        │       │                   client name to crash krb5kdc and deny authentication. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       │                   7cc4226866b71 
│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: krb5: Denial of Service via crafted forwarded
│                        │       │                   credentials 
│                        │       ├ Description     : MIT Kerberos 5 (krb5) through 1.22.2 contains a NULL
│                        │       │                   pointer dereference in make_cred_list() in rd_cred.c that
│                        │       │                   allows authenticated Kerberos clients to crash services by
│                        │       │                    sending mismatched KRB-CRED arrays. Attackers can send
│                        │       │                   forwarded credentials with more tickets than ticket_info
│                        │       │                   entries through gss_accept_sec_context() to crash GSS-API
│                        │       │                   acceptor services, causing denial of service. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       │                   2966213e3ea6a 
│                        │       ├ Title           : krb5: integer overflow in dbentry->n_key_data in
│                        │       │                   kadmin/dbutil/dump.c 
│                        │       ├ Description     : An issue was discovered in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5)
│                        │       │                   through 1.16. There is a variable "dbentry->n_key_data" in
│                        │       │                    kadmin/dbutil/dump.c that can store 16-bit data but
│                        │       │                   unknowingly the developer has assigned a "u4" variable to
│                        │       │                   it, which is for 32-bit data. An attacker can use this
│                        │       │                   vulnerability to affect other artifacts of the database as
│                        │       │                    we know that a Kerberos database dump file contains
│                        │       │                   trusted data.

│                        │       │                   e5088c4c3153e 
│                        │       ├ Title           : acl: Symlink traversal privilege escalation via libacl
│                        │       │                   functions 
│                        │       ├ Description     : acl before version 2.4.0 contains a symlink traversal
│                        │       │                   vulnerability in the libacl pathname-based functions
│                        │       │                   acl_get_file(), acl_set_file(), acl_extended_file(), and
│                        │       │                   acl_delete_def_file() that allows local attackers to
│                        │       │                   escalate privileges by replacing any pathname component
│                        │       │                   with a symbolic link. Attackers who control any component
│                        │       │                   of a pathname processed by a privileged caller can
│                        │       │                   redirect ACL read or write operations to arbitrary files
│                        │       │                   or directories, enabling unauthorized manipulation of
│                        │       │                   access control lists and local privilege escalation.

│                        │       │                   b207dc4d8f2df 
│                        │       ├ Title           : acl: TOCTOU Symlink Traversal via getfacl/setfacl 
│                        │       ├ Description     : acl before version 2.4.0 contains a time-of-check to
│                        │       │                   time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition vulnerability that
│                        │       │                   allows local attackers to escalate privileges by replacing
│                        │       │                    a pathname component with a symbolic link between an
│                        │       │                   lstat() check and subsequent symlink-following operations
│                        │       │                   such as stat(), chown(), chmod(), acl_get_file(), and
│                        │       │                   acl_set_file(). Attackers who control a pathname component
│                        │       │                    can redirect file access control list operations to
│                        │       │                   arbitrary files when getfacl, setfacl, or chacl is invoked
│                        │       │                    by a privileged process over an attacker-controlled path,
│                        │       │                    resulting in local privilege escalation.

│                        │       ├ Title           : attr: attr: Symlink Traversal Privilege Escalation via
│                        │       │                   getfattr and setfattr 
│                        │       ├ Description     : attr before version 2.6.0 contains a symlink traversal
│                        │       │                   vulnerability in the getfattr and setfattr utilities that
│                        │       │                   allows local attackers to escalate privileges by replacing
│                        │       │                    a pathname component with a symbolic link during
│                        │       │                   directory hierarchy traversal. Attackers who control a
│                        │       │                   pathname component can redirect getfattr and setfattr
│                        │       │                   operations to arbitrary files by substituting a symlink,
│                        │       │                   leading to local privilege escalation when getfattr or
│                        │       │                   setfattr is invoked by a privileged process over an
│                        │       │                   attacker-controlled path.

│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: failed external mount helper still
│                        │       │                    runs privileged X-mount post-hooks 
│                        │       ├ Description     : util-linux versions through 2.41.5 and 2.42.2 fail to
│                        │       │                   check mount helper exit status before running post-mount
│                        │       │                   hooks, allowing unprivileged users to execute privileged
│                        │       │                   operations on pre-existing filesystems. Attackers can
│                        │       │                   exploit X-mount.idmap or X-mount.owner hooks to clone
│                        │       │                   filesystems with inherited suid bits or modify target
│                        │       │                   inode permissions after a helper fails, achieving
│                        │       │                   privilege escalation.

│                        │       │                   665a0425e37e1 
│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: nsenter --join-cgroup leaks root
│                        │       │                   cgroup migration authority 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The nsenter --join-cgroup option opens the target
│                        │       │                   cgroup.procs file as root and leaves that file descriptor
│                        │       │                   open across later namespace and credential changes and
│                        │       │                   across execve(). Because the kernel checks later cgroup
│                        │       │                   migrations using the credentials from the original open, a
│                        │       │                    program run in an attacker-controlled target can inherit
│                        │       │                   root's ability to move host processes between cgroups.
│                        │       │                   After a privileged operator uses --join-cgroup against
│                        │       │                   that target, an unprivileged user can migrate and
│                        │       │                   terminate unrelated root processes.

│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: X-mount.subdir detached-tree
│                        │       │                   resolution can escape via intermediate symlinks 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The X-mount.subdir option uses a detached-tree fast path
│                        │       │                   on Linux 6.15 and later and passes the configured
│                        │       │                   subdirectory to open_tree() with AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW. That
│                        │       │                    flag does not stop intermediate symlink traversal or keep
│                        │       │                    resolution inside the newly mounted filesystem. A local
│                        │       │                   unprivileged user with an fstab-authorized X-mount.subdir
│                        │       │                   entry can attach a host path at the intended mountpoint.[

│                        │       │                   c4c698026ca60 
│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: restricted bind mounts do not pin
│                        │       │                   the source, allowing X-mount.owner/group/mode
│                        │       │                   redirection 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in util-linux. Restricted bind mounts
│                        │       │                   take the source path from fstab but do not pin that source
│                        │       │                    before the privileged mount. A local unprivileged user
│                        │       │                   who can replace the authorized source or a writable
│                        │       │                   ancestor can redirect SUID mount(8) to bind another host
│                        │       │                   directory. If the fstab entry also sets X-mount.owner,
│                        │       │                   X-mount.group, or X-mount.mode, root then changes
│                        │       │                   ownership or mode on that redirected inode.

│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: Access control bypass due to
│                        │       │                   improper hostname canonicalization 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in util-linux. Improper hostname
│                        │       │                   canonicalization in the `login(1)` utility, when invoked
│                        │       │                   with the `-h` option, can modify the supplied remote
│                        │       │                   hostname before setting `PAM_RHOST`. A remote attacker
│                        │       │                   could exploit this by providing a specially crafted
│                        │       │                   hostname, potentially bypassing host-based Pluggable
│                        │       │                   Authentication Modules (PAM) access control rules that
│                        │       │                   rely on fully qualified domain names. This could lead to
│                        │       │                   unauthorized access.

│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: partial disclosure of arbitrary files in chfn
│                        │       │                   and chsh when compiled with libreadline 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in the util-linux chfn and chsh utilities
│                        │       │                    when compiled with Readline support. The Readline library
│                        │       │                    uses an "INPUTRC" environment variable to get a path to
│                        │       │                   the library config file. When the library cannot parse the
│                        │       │                    specified file, it prints an error message containing
│                        │       │                   data from the file. This flaw allows an unprivileged user
│                        │       │                   to read root-owned files, potentially leading to privilege
│                        │       │                    escalation. This flaw affects util-linux versions prior
│                        │       │                   to 2.37.4.

│                        │       │                   1d154d89d372d 
│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: glibc: Memory corruption via out-of-bounds write in
│                        │       │                    wide scanf functions 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Calling the wide scanf family of functions (swscanf,
│                        │       │                   fwscanf, wscanf, vswscanf, vfwscanf and vwscanf) with a %s
│                        │       │                    or %[ conversion without the 'l' length modifier in the
│                        │       │                   GNU C Library version 2.2 to version 2.44 writes an extra
│                        │       │                   null byte one past the end of the destination array when
│                        │       │                   the converted multibyte string and its terminating null
│                        │       │                   byte exactly fill that array.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   These conversions store each wide input character into the
│                        │       │                    caller's char array as a multibyte sequence.  The
│                        │       │                   conversion ends with the sequence that returns to the
│                        │       │                   initial shift state, which also stores the terminating
│                        │       │                   null byte, and the functions then append a second null
│                        │       │                   byte.  A destination sized for the converted string and
│                        │       │                   one terminator, as the C standard requires the caller to
│                        │       │                   provide, is therefore written one byte past its end.  The
│                        │       │                   out-of-bounds byte is always a null byte, which may
│                        │       │                   corrupt adjacent data or crash the process.  An attacker
│                        │       │                   who supplies the input can trigger the overflow with a
│                        │       │                   string whose converted length exactly fills the
│                        │       │                   destination.
│                        │       │                   The narrow scanf functions, the %ls and %l[ conversions
│                        │       │                   into a wchar_t array, and the 'a' and 'm' allocation
│                        │       │                   modifiers are not affected, and storing a wide scanf
│                        │       │                   conversion into a narrow char array is uncommon.  This
│                        │       │                   issue affects all architectures and ABIs supported by the
│                        │       │                   GNU C Library.

│                        │       │                   6ed23b0125454 
│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: glibc: Denial of Service via out-of-bounds read in
│                        │       │                   CP949 character conversion 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Converting crafted CP949 input to UTF-8 character encoding
│                        │       │                    and ignoring invalid characters, in the GNU C Library
│                        │       │                   version 2.1 or later may result in the converter reading
│                        │       │                   past the end of the input buffer, causing the calling
│                        │       │                   application to crash.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   When the CP949 decoder encounters an invalid input byte
│                        │       │                   sequence like '\xa2\xe8' it ends up advancing the pointer
│                        │       │                   tracking the read buffer position twice.  If //IGNORE is
│                        │       │                   set on the destination encoding and this sequence is at
│                        │       │                   the end of the input buffer, the decoder may then end up
│                        │       │                   reading past the bounds of the input buffer.  To exploit
│                        │       │                   this, the target iconv function needs to set //IGNORE on
│                        │       │                   the destination of the conversion and the input and
│                        │       │                   encoding needs to be attacker controlled.

│                        │       │                   996077f646e46 
│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: glibc: Arbitrary code execution via directory
│                        │       │                   traversal in LANGUAGE environment variable 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The gettext family of functions in the GNU C Library
│                        │       │                   version 2.0 and later accept LANGUAGE environment variable
│                        │       │                    entries that contain '/' or that are equal to "..",
│                        │       │                   unless the program is setuid or setgid (AT_SECURE).  An
│                        │       │                   attacker who can set LANGUAGE in the environment of a
│                        │       │                   program that uses gettext can make it load a message
│                        │       │                   catalog (.mo file) from an arbitrary location in the file
│                        │       │                   system.  A crafted .mo file can crash the program through
│                        │       │                   out-of-range offsets, or supply translations whose format
│                        │       │                   directives do not match the arguments passed by the
│                        │       │                   program.  That causes undefined behaviour in the printf
│                        │       │                   family of functions and may allow arbitrary code execution
│                        │       │                    with the privileges of the program.  The safety of
│                        │       │                   message catalogs relies on them being installed in
│                        │       │                   trusted, read-only locations, and the directory traversal
│                        │       │                   bypasses this.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   The fix for CVE-2014-0475 rejects ".." path components in
│                        │       │                   locale names passed to setlocale or taken from the LC_ALL,
│                        │       │                    LC_* and LANG environment variables.  gettext reads
│                        │       │                   LANGUAGE directly and appends each colon-separated entry
│                        │       │                   to the message catalog directory, so that fix did not
│                        │       │                   cover LANGUAGE.
│                        │       │                   LANGUAGE is only used when the LC_MESSAGES locale is not
│                        │       │                   "C", "C.<encoding>" or "POSIX", so the attacker must also
│                        │       │                   be able to select another installed locale, for example
│                        │       │                   through LANG or LC_ALL.  Exploitation also requires that
│                        │       │                   the attacker can place the crafted file in a location
│                        │       │                   readable by the target program, and that the environment
│                        │       │                   crosses a trust boundary without the program running as
│                        │       │                   AT_SECURE.  An example is an SSH server that accepts
│                        │       │                   LANGUAGE and LANG from clients through the AcceptEnv
│                        │       │                   directive and restricts an account to a forced command;
│                        │       │                   the attacker may use this to escape the restriction.

│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: glob implementation can cause excessive CPU and
│                        │       │                   memory consumption due to crafted glob expressions 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The glob implementation in the GNU C Library (aka glibc or
│                        │       │                    libc6) allows remote authenticated users to cause a
│                        │       │                   denial of service (CPU and memory consumption) via crafted
│                        │       │                    glob expressions that do not match any pathnames, as
│                        │       │                   demonstrated by glob expressions in STAT commands to an
│                        │       │                   FTP daemon, a different vulnerability than
│                        │       │                   CVE-2010-2632.

│                        │       │                   bb5a8ae52b928 
│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: glibc: Denial of Service via memory allocation
│                        │       │                   failure during regular expression processing 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The regcomp and regexec functions in the GNU C Library
│                        │       │                   version 2.3 to version 2.44 may read freed memory and free
│                        │       │                    the same heap block twice when a memory allocation fails
│                        │       │                   while a regular expression is compiled or matched.  The
│                        │       │                   re_dfa_add_node (the NFA node table) and build_range_exp
│                        │       │                   (bracket ranges) grow several arrays with consecutive
│                        │       │                   realloc calls and store the new pointers only after all of
│                        │       │                    them succeed.  When a later call fails, the pattern
│                        │       │                   buffer keeps pointers to blocks that were already freed,
│                        │       │                   and the error cleanup frees them again.  In regexec, the
│                        │       │                   back-reference cache (match_ctx_add_entry) frees its array
│                        │       │                    when a realloc fails but keeps the pointer, which is
│                        │       │                   freed again on the error path.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   An attacker does not need to supply a crafted regular
│                        │       │                   expression: patterns large enough to grow these arrays are
│                        │       │                    common.  The failure has to hit a specific allocation,
│                        │       │                   though, so the issue can only be reached when the system
│                        │       │                   is already under memory pressure.  An attacker who
│                        │       │                   supplies the pattern or the subject string has little
│                        │       │                   control over which allocation fails, so the expected
│                        │       │                   impact is a crash of the process.  This issue affects all
│                        │       │                   architectures and ABIs supported by the GNU C Library.
