│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: X-mount.subdir detached-tree
│                        │       │                   resolution can escape via intermediate symlinks 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The X-mount.subdir option uses a detached-tree fast path
│                        │       │                   on Linux 6.15 and later and passes the configured
│                        │       │                   subdirectory to open_tree() with AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW. That
│                        │       │                    flag does not stop intermediate symlink traversal or keep
│                        │       │                    resolution inside the newly mounted filesystem. A local
│                        │       │                   unprivileged user with an fstab-authorized X-mount.subdir
│                        │       │                   entry can attach a host path at the intended mountpoint.[

│                        │       │                   f36499a6fc29a 
│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: restricted bind mounts do not pin
│                        │       │                   the source, allowing X-mount.owner/group/mode
│                        │       │                   redirection 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in util-linux. Restricted bind mounts
│                        │       │                   take the source path from fstab but do not pin that source
│                        │       │                    before the privileged mount. A local unprivileged user
│                        │       │                   who can replace the authorized source or a writable
│                        │       │                   ancestor can redirect SUID mount(8) to bind another host
│                        │       │                   directory. If the fstab entry also sets X-mount.owner,
│                        │       │                   X-mount.group, or X-mount.mode, root then changes
│                        │       │                   ownership or mode on that redirected inode.

│                        │       │                   3e69298070dd0 
│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: Access control bypass due to
│                        │       │                   improper hostname canonicalization 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in util-linux. Improper hostname
│                        │       │                   canonicalization in the `login(1)` utility, when invoked
│                        │       │                   with the `-h` option, can modify the supplied remote
│                        │       │                   hostname before setting `PAM_RHOST`. A remote attacker
│                        │       │                   could exploit this by providing a specially crafted
│                        │       │                   hostname, potentially bypassing host-based Pluggable
│                        │       │                   Authentication Modules (PAM) access control rules that
│                        │       │                   rely on fully qualified domain names. This could lead to
│                        │       │                   unauthorized access.

│                        │       │                   90627fb230eb9 
│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: partial disclosure of arbitrary files in chfn
│                        │       │                   and chsh when compiled with libreadline 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in the util-linux chfn and chsh utilities
│                        │       │                    when compiled with Readline support. The Readline library
│                        │       │                    uses an "INPUTRC" environment variable to get a path to
│                        │       │                   the library config file. When the library cannot parse the
│                        │       │                    specified file, it prints an error message containing
│                        │       │                   data from the file. This flaw allows an unprivileged user
│                        │       │                   to read root-owned files, potentially leading to privilege
│                        │       │                    escalation. This flaw affects util-linux versions prior
│                        │       │                   to 2.37.4.

│                        │       ├ Title           : gnu-ncurses: ncurses Stack Buffer Overflow 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A vulnerability has been found in GNU ncurses up to
│                        │       │                   6.5-20250322 and classified as problematic. This
│                        │       │                   vulnerability affects the function postprocess_termcap of
│                        │       │                   the file tinfo/parse_entry.c. The manipulation leads to
│                        │       │                   stack-based buffer overflow. The attack needs to be
│                        │       │                   approached locally. Upgrading to version 6.5-20250329 is
│                        │       │                   able to address this issue. It is recommended to upgrade
│                        │       │                   the affected component.

│                        │       │                   cba055cf36181 
│                        │       ├ Title           : p11-kit: Stack exhaustion via unbounded recursion in RPC
│                        │       │                   attribute parsing 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in p11-kit. The RPC message attribute
│                        │       │                   parsing functions p11_rpc_message_get_attribute() and
│                        │       │                   p11_rpc_message_get_attribute_array_value() form a
│                        │       │                   mutually-recursive call chain with no recursion depth
│                        │       │                   limit when processing nested CKA_WRAP_TEMPLATE,
│                        │       │                   CKA_UNWRAP_TEMPLATE, and CKA_DERIVE_TEMPLATE attributes.
│                        │       │                   An unauthenticated attacker with local access to the
│                        │       │                   p11-kit RPC Unix domain socket can send a specially
│                        │       │                   crafted request with deeply nested template attributes,
│                        │       │                   causing stack exhaustion and crashing the p11-kit server
│                        │       │                   process and its dependent services.

│                        │       │                   6366e63108618 
│                        │       ├ Title           : p11-kit: Integer overflow in RPC attribute-array length
│                        │       │                   calculation can under-allocate nested attribute storage on
│                        │       │                    32 bit systems 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in p11-kit. A local attacker, or one with
│                        │       │                    equivalent access to a reachable RPC channel, could
│                        │       │                   exploit an integer overflow vulnerability. By sending
│                        │       │                   specially crafted messages, the attacker can cause the
│                        │       │                   system to miscalculate memory allocation for nested
│                        │       │                   attributes. This leads to a memory corruption issue,
│                        │       │                   specifically a heap out-of-bounds write, which can crash
│                        │       │                   the p11-kit RPC parsing process, resulting in a Denial of
│                        │       │                   Service (DoS). This vulnerability is only exploitable on
│                        │       │                   32 bit systems. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       ├ Title           : linux-pam: Plaintext password recovery via timing
│                        │       │                   discrepancy in pam_userdb module 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Linux-PAM through 1.7.2 contains an observable timing
│                        │       │                   discrepancy (CWE-208) in the pam_userdb module's
│                        │       │                   plaintext-password comparison path in
│                        │       │                   modules/pam_userdb/pam_userdb.c that allows a local or
│                        │       │                   network-adjacent attacker able to repeatedly drive
│                        │       │                   authentication through a calling service to recover the
│                        │       │                   plaintext password of a target account by measuring
│                        │       │                   response-timing differences.

│                        │       ├ Title           : linux-pam: Plaintext password recovery via timing
│                        │       │                   discrepancy in pam_userdb module 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Linux-PAM through 1.7.2 contains an observable timing
│                        │       │                   discrepancy (CWE-208) in the pam_userdb module's
│                        │       │                   plaintext-password comparison path in
│                        │       │                   modules/pam_userdb/pam_userdb.c that allows a local or
│                        │       │                   network-adjacent attacker able to repeatedly drive
│                        │       │                   authentication through a calling service to recover the
│                        │       │                   plaintext password of a target account by measuring
│                        │       │                   response-timing differences.

│                        │       ├ Title           : perl-Archive-Tar: perl-Archive-Tar: Denial of Service via
│                        │       │                   crafted tar header with large entry size 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Archive::Tar versions before 3.10 for Perl allow memory
│                        │       │                   exhaustion via attacker controlled entry size field in tar
│                        │       │                    header.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   _read_tar() reads each entry's payload with
│                        │       │                   $handle->read($$data, $block), where $block is derived
│                        │       │                   from the entry's 12-byte size field in the tar header with
│                        │       │                    no upper bound on that value.
│                        │       │                   A crafted header declaring a multi-gigabyte size causes
│                        │       │                   Perl to allocate a scalar of that size.

│                        │       │                   255f65ee81eff 
│                        │       ├ Title           : perl: Perl: Arbitrary code execution via out-of-bounds
│                        │       │                   memory access in regular expression engine. 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Perl versions through 5.45.1 have out-of-bounds heap reads
│                        │       │                    and writes during regular expression matching via an
│                        │       │                   undersized superlinear cache in S_regmatch.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   The regex engine's superlinear cache holds one bit per
│                        │       │                   subject position for each participating WHILEM node, so
│                        │       │                   the bit count is the subject length plus one times the
│                        │       │                   number of nodes. Nothing checks that product for positive
│                        │       │                   overflow of the signed 32-bit count: a 286331153 byte
│                        │       │                   subject matched against a pattern with 15 participating
│                        │       │                   nodes stores the count as 14, leaving a two byte cache.
│                        │       │                   The cache is then indexed from the real match position and
│                        │       │                    node number, so reads go past the end of the allocation,
│                        │       │                   and on failure CACHEsayNO sets a bit past it.
│                        │       │                   A caller that matches an attacker controlled subject of
│                        │       │                   this size against a pattern of this shape can crash the
│                        │       │                   process or corrupt heap memory.

│                        │       ├ Title           : Pod::Text versions before 6.1.1 for Perl allow CPU and
│                        │       │                   memory exhausti ... 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Pod::Text versions before 6.1.1 for Perl allow CPU and
│                        │       │                   memory exhaustion formatting a POD document whose =over
│                        │       │                   nesting drives the margin to the output width.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   Each =over adds its indent to the margin, which wrap()
│                        │       │                   subtracts from the output width to get the space available
│                        │       │                    for text. When that space reaches zero, the
│                        │       │                   line-splitting substitution matches the empty string, and
│                        │       │                   the loop consumes no input while appending the margin
│                        │       │                   padding on every pass.
│                        │       │                   Formatting an attacker-supplied POD document never
│                        │       │                   returns, and the output grows until memory is exhausted.[

│                        │       │                   75235e5fb23a8 
│                        │       ├ Title           : cyrus-sasl: Heap buffer overflow in cyrus-sasl
│                        │       │                   add_to_challenge() allows malicious server to crash or
│                        │       │                   compromise DIGEST-MD5 clients 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A heap-based buffer overflow flaw was found in Cyrus SASL.
│                        │       │                    The add_to_challenge() function in the DIGEST-MD5 plugin
│                        │       │                   computes the size of the buffer needed for a
│                        │       │                   challenge/response field before DIGEST-MD5 quoting is
│                        │       │                   applied, but does not recompute that size when quoting
│                        │       │                   (escaping special characters) makes the value longer. The
│                        │       │                   under-sized buffer is then passed to strcat(), causing a
│                        │       │                   heap-based out-of-bounds write whose size depends on
│                        │       │                   attacker-controlled input. A malicious or on-path
│                        │       │                   DIGEST-MD5 (or HTTP Digest) server can trigger this flaw
│                        │       │                   in a connecting client by supplying a crafted challenge
│                        │       │                   field, such as realm or nonce, most likely resulting in a
│                        │       │                   crash of the client application.

│                        │       ├ Title           : cyrus-sasl: Cyrus SASL through 2.1.28 SRP Authentication
│                        │       │                   Bypass via plugins/srp.c 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Cyrus SASL through 2.1.28 contains an authentication
│                        │       │                   bypass vulnerability in the SRP server mechanism because
│                        │       │                   srp_server_mech_step2 does not reject client public values
│                        │       │                    A that are multiples of N. Unauthenticated network
│                        │       │                   clients can send A equal to N to force a zero shared
│                        │       │                   secret, authenticating as any existing user without the
│                        │       │                   password and learning session keys.

│                        │       ├ Description     : Cyrus SASL through 2.1.28 contains an authentication
│                        │       │                   bypass vulnerability in the SRP server mechanism because
│                        │       │                   srp_server_mech_step2 does not reject client public values
│                        │       │                    A that are multiples of N. Unauthenticated network
│                        │       │                   clients can send A equal to N to force a zero shared
│                        │       │                   secret, authenticating as any existing user without the
│                        │       │                   password and learning session keys.

│                        │       │                   7d8d0608762f0 
│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: nsenter --join-cgroup leaks root
│                        │       │                   cgroup migration authority 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The nsenter --join-cgroup option opens the target
│                        │       │                   cgroup.procs file as root and leaves that file descriptor
│                        │       │                   open across later namespace and credential changes and
│                        │       │                   across execve(). Because the kernel checks later cgroup
│                        │       │                   migrations using the credentials from the original open, a
│                        │       │                    program run in an attacker-controlled target can inherit
│                        │       │                   root's ability to move host processes between cgroups.
│                        │       │                   After a privileged operator uses --join-cgroup against
│                        │       │                   that target, an unprivileged user can migrate and
│                        │       │                   terminate unrelated root processes.

│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: X-mount.subdir detached-tree
│                        │       │                   resolution can escape via intermediate symlinks 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The X-mount.subdir option uses a detached-tree fast path
│                        │       │                   on Linux 6.15 and later and passes the configured
│                        │       │                   subdirectory to open_tree() with AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW. That
│                        │       │                    flag does not stop intermediate symlink traversal or keep
│                        │       │                    resolution inside the newly mounted filesystem. A local
│                        │       │                   unprivileged user with an fstab-authorized X-mount.subdir
│                        │       │                   entry can attach a host path at the intended mountpoint.[

│                        │       │                   f3dac7fc5b03e 
│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: restricted bind mounts do not pin
│                        │       │                   the source, allowing X-mount.owner/group/mode
│                        │       │                   redirection 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in util-linux. Restricted bind mounts
│                        │       │                   take the source path from fstab but do not pin that source
│                        │       │                    before the privileged mount. A local unprivileged user
│                        │       │                   who can replace the authorized source or a writable
│                        │       │                   ancestor can redirect SUID mount(8) to bind another host
│                        │       │                   directory. If the fstab entry also sets X-mount.owner,
│                        │       │                   X-mount.group, or X-mount.mode, root then changes
│                        │       │                   ownership or mode on that redirected inode.

│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: Access control bypass due to
│                        │       │                   improper hostname canonicalization 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in util-linux. Improper hostname
│                        │       │                   canonicalization in the `login(1)` utility, when invoked
│                        │       │                   with the `-h` option, can modify the supplied remote
│                        │       │                   hostname before setting `PAM_RHOST`. A remote attacker
│                        │       │                   could exploit this by providing a specially crafted
│                        │       │                   hostname, potentially bypassing host-based Pluggable
│                        │       │                   Authentication Modules (PAM) access control rules that
│                        │       │                   rely on fully qualified domain names. This could lead to
│                        │       │                   unauthorized access.

│                        │       │                   a1b5654d67db0 
│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: partial disclosure of arbitrary files in chfn
│                        │       │                   and chsh when compiled with libreadline 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in the util-linux chfn and chsh utilities
│                        │       │                    when compiled with Readline support. The Readline library
│                        │       │                    uses an "INPUTRC" environment variable to get a path to
│                        │       │                   the library config file. When the library cannot parse the
│                        │       │                    specified file, it prints an error message containing
│                        │       │                   data from the file. This flaw allows an unprivileged user
│                        │       │                   to read root-owned files, potentially leading to privilege
│                        │       │                    escalation. This flaw affects util-linux versions prior
│                        │       │                   to 2.37.4.

│                        │       │                   54d623e681a68 
│                        │       ├ Title           : sqlite: sqlite: Denial of service via heap-based buffer
│                        │       │                   overflow in FTS5 
│                        │       ├ Description     : SQLite before 3.54.0 built with FTS5 contains a heap
│                        │       │                   buffer overflow in fts5MergeRowidLists() that undersizes
│                        │       │                   the output buffer when merging detail=none prefix
│                        │       │                   doclists. Attackers who can populate a detail=none FTS5
│                        │       │                   table with negative rowids and run a prefix MATCH query
│                        │       │                   can write past the allocation, corrupting heap memory and
│                        │       │                   crashing the process.

│                        │       │                   3afe42b461097 
│                        │       ├ Title           : sqlite: sqlite: Arbitrary code execution via corrupted
│                        │       │                   FTS5 index 
│                        │       ├ Description     : SQLite before 3.54.0 built with FTS5 contains a heap
│                        │       │                   buffer overflow in fts5DoSecureDelete() that allows
│                        │       │                   attackers to write past the leaf page buffer via crafted
│                        │       │                   footer key offsets. Attackers can supply a database file
│                        │       │                   with a corrupted FTS5 index that, when deleted from with
│                        │       │                   secure-delete enabled, corrupts heap memory and crashes
│                        │       │                   the application.

│                        │       ├ Title           : sqlite: sqlite: Arbitrary code execution via crafted
│                        │       │                   session changesets 
│                        │       ├ Description     : SQLite before 3.54.0 built with the session extension
│                        │       │                   contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in
│                        │       │                   sqlite3changeset_apply() that allows attackers to corrupt
│                        │       │                   heap memory by supplying crafted changesets. Attackers can
│                        │       │                    repeat a table name in a second changeset block with a
│                        │       │                   larger column count, causing sessionUpdateFind() to memset
│                        │       │                    past the undersized aUpdateMask allocation.

│                        │       │                   00e3f253b6fe2 
│                        │       ├ Title           : sqlite: sqlite: Denial of Service via stack exhaustion
│                        │       │                   from deeply nested Common Table Expressions 
│                        │       ├ Description     : SQLite before 3.54.0 contains a stack exhaustion
│                        │       │                   vulnerability that allows attackers to bypass the
│                        │       │                   SQLITE_LIMIT_EXPR_DEPTH nesting limit because common table
│                        │       │                    expressions are not counted against it. Attackers can
│                        │       │                   supply a WITH clause chaining tens of thousands of CTEs,
│                        │       │                   via plain SQL or a view in an untrusted database file,
│                        │       │                   causing unbounded selectExpander() recursion that crashes
│                        │       │                   the process. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       │                   47151a03d3500 
│                        │       ├ Title           : sqlite: sqlite: Denial of Service via use-after-free in
│                        │       │                   full-text search 
│                        │       ├ Description     : SQLite before 3.54.0 built with FTS3/FTS4 and
│                        │       │                   SQLITE_ENABLE_FTS3_PARENTHESIS contains a use-after-free
│                        │       │                   vulnerability in fts3BestSnippet() caused by dangling
│                        │       │                   cached position-list pointers. Attackers can run a
│                        │       │                   full-text MATCH query combining OR and NEAR operators with
│                        │       │                    snippet() to read freed heap memory and crash the
│                        │       │                   process. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       ├ Title           : sqlite: sqlite: Information disclosure via undersized WAL
│                        │       │                   page size 
│                        │       ├ Description     : SQLite before 3.54.0 contains an information disclosure
│                        │       │                   vulnerability that allows attackers to read uninitialized
│                        │       │                   page-cache memory by supplying a WAL file with an
│                        │       │                   undersized page size. Attackers can craft a database and
│                        │       │                   WAL file whose oversized record payload makes queries like
│                        │       │                    substr() return stale bytes, disclosing other table rows
│                        │       │                   and internal pointers. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       │                   445edabf60025 
│                        │       ├ Title           : sqlite: sqlite: Denial of Service via stack exhaustion
│                        │       │                   from chained COLLATE operators 
│                        │       ├ Description     : SQLite before 3.54.0 contains a stack exhaustion
│                        │       │                   vulnerability that allows attackers to bypass the
│                        │       │                   SQLITE_LIMIT_EXPR_DEPTH limit by chaining COLLATE postfix
│                        │       │                   operators. Attackers can supply roughly 175,000 chained
│                        │       │                   COLLATE operators in SQL or an untrusted database view to
│                        │       │                   trigger unbounded recursion in sqlite3WalkExprNN() and
│                        │       │                   crash the process. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       │                   0a157f4f5bd47 
│                        │       ├ Title           : sqlite: sqlite: Denial of Service via use-after-free in
│                        │       │                   R-Tree extension 
│                        │       ├ Description     : SQLite before 3.54.0 contains a use-after-free
│                        │       │                   vulnerability in the R-Tree extension that allows
│                        │       │                   attackers to make applications use freed heap memory by
│                        │       │                   manipulating the %_node shadow table. Attackers can supply
│                        │       │                    a database declaring %_node WITHOUT ROWID or with a
│                        │       │                   RAISE(IGNORE) trigger so nodeWrite() hashes nodes as 0,
│                        │       │                   crashing the process after node splits. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       │                   1cc3f7644b624 
│                        │       ├ Title           : sqlite: sqlite: Denial of Service via stack exhaustion in
│                        │       │                   countOfViewOptimization() 
│                        │       ├ Description     : SQLite before 3.54.0 contains a stack exhaustion
│                        │       │                   vulnerability in countOfViewOptimization() that allows
│                        │       │                   attackers to crash the host process via count(*) over a
│                        │       │                   large multi-row VALUES clause. Attackers supplying SQL or
│                        │       │                   a database file with a crafted view can trigger deeply
│                        │       │                   nested TK_PLUS expressions whose recursive freeing in
│                        │       │                   sqlite3ExprDeleteNN() exhausts the C stack, causing denial
│                        │       │                    of service. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       ├ Title           : sqlite: SQLite: Denial of Service via malformed changeset
│                        │       │                   in Session Extension 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A NULL pointer dereference in the SQLite Session Extension
│                        │       │                    in SQLite 3.53.1 and SQLite trunk builds before check-in
│                        │       │                   e807d4e3798efd53 allows an attacker who can supply a
│                        │       │                   malformed changeset blob to cause a denial of service. The
│                        │       │                    issue occurs when sqlite3changeset_apply_v3() applies a
│                        │       │                   corrupt changeset and reaches sqlite3_value_type() with a
│                        │       │                   NULL sqlite3_value pointer.

│                        │       ├ Title           : sqlite: crafted SQL query allows a malicious user to
│                        │       │                   obtain sensitive information 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A Memory Leak vulnerability exists in SQLite Project
│                        │       │                   SQLite3 3.35.1 and 3.37.0 via maliciously crafted SQL
│                        │       │                   Queries (made via editing the Database File), it is
│                        │       │                   possible to query a record, and leak subsequent bytes of
│                        │       │                   memory that extend beyond the record, which could let a
│                        │       │                   malicious user obtain sensitive information. NOTE: The
│                        │       │                   developer disputes this as a vulnerability stating that If
│                        │       │                    you give SQLite a corrupted database file and submit a
│                        │       │                   query against the database, it might read parts of the
│                        │       │                   database that you did not intend or expect.

│                        │       ├ Title           : sqlite: sqlite: Authorization bypass via USING clause in
│                        │       │                   JOIN queries 
│                        │       ├ Description     : SQLite before 3.54.0 contains an authorization bypass
│                        │       │                   vulnerability in lookupName() that invokes the authorizer
│                        │       │                   only for the first joined table's USING column. Attackers
│                        │       │                   able to submit SQL can query a shared USING column in a
│                        │       │                   RIGHT or FULL JOIN to read columns denied via
│                        │       │                   sqlite3_set_authorizer() SQLITE_READ restrictions.

│                        │       │                   2391dd8b1ad7d 
│                        │       ├ Title           : openssl: OpenSSL: Denial of Service via unbounded QUIC
│                        │       │                   frame queueing 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Issue summary: The QUIC stack queues a
│                        │       │                   RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame also for
│                        │       │                   retransmitted NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames. This allows a
│                        │       │                   remote malicious
│                        │       │                   QUIC stack to queue an unlimited number of
│                        │       │                   RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   Impact summary: A malicious remote QUIC peer can trigger
│                        │       │                   an out-of-memory
│                        │       │                   condition causing a Denial of Service.
│                        │       │                   CWE: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or
│                        │       │                   Throttling
│                        │       │                   Description: The earlier fix for CVE-2026-84784 was not
│                        │       │                   complete. It
│                        │       │                   failed to ignore retransmissions of the NEW_CONNECTION_ID
│                        │       │                   frame. The QUIC
│                        │       │                   implementation created and inserted a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID
│                        │       │                    frame for every
│                        │       │                   retransmitted NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame it received and
│                        │       │                   there was no limit
│                        │       │                   on how many RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames were queued.
│                        │       │                   This issue allows a malicious remote QUIC stack to trigger
│                        │       │                    an unbounded
│                        │       │                   allocation of memory and eventually an out-of-memory (OOM)
│                        │       │                    condition.
│                        │       │                   FIPS impact: no
│                        │       │                   The FIPS module is not affected as the QUIC implementation
│                        │       │                    is outside the
│                        │       │                   OpenSSL FIPS module boundary.

│                        │       │                   f771df07fb6b4 
│                        │       ├ Title           : openssl: openssl: Denial of Service via memory leak in
│                        │       │                   QUIC stream handling 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Issue summary: A QUIC server that rejects a stream opened
│                        │       │                   by the peer may
│                        │       │                   retain that stream's state for the lifetime of the
│                        │       │                   connection if the peer
│                        │       │                   resets the stream before the rejection is signalled, even
│                        │       │                   though the peer's
│                        │       │                   stream credit is returned.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   Impact summary: A remote client that completes a QUIC
│                        │       │                   handshake can repeatedly
│                        │       │                   open and reset streams, causing server memory to grow
│                        │       │                   without bound until the
│                        │       │                   process runs out of memory and every connection on it is
│                        │       │                   lost. This is a
│                        │       │                   Denial of Service.
│                        │       │                   CWE: CWE-401: Missing Release of Memory after Effective
│                        │       │                   Lifetime
│                        │       │                   Description: QUIC servers track each stream the peer
│                        │       │                   opens. When the incoming
│                        │       │                   stream policy rejects a stream, OpenSSL schedules a
│                        │       │                   STOP_SENDING frame, marks
│                        │       │                   the stream deleted and returns the peer's stream credit. A
│                        │       │                    deleted stream is
│                        │       │                   collected only once its receive part is fully drained,
│                        │       │                   which for a rejected
│                        │       │                   stream means the STOP_SENDING has been acknowledged. If
│                        │       │                   the peer sends
│                        │       │                   RESET_STREAM first, the reset cancels the pending
│                        │       │                   STOP_SENDING, so it is never
│                        │       │                   sent or acknowledged and the stream is never collected.
│                        │       │                   The default configuration reaches this path. Once a
│                        │       │                   connection has a default
│                        │       │                   stream, meaning the application has read from or written
│                        │       │                   to the connection as
│                        │       │                   the tutorial server does, the effective incoming stream
│                        │       │                   policy rejects streams
│                        │       │                   the application does not accept. Applications that set the
│                        │       │                    REJECT policy
│                        │       │                   explicitly are affected too.
│                        │       │                   Each retained stream costs about 300 bytes, and the peer's
│                        │       │                    stream credit
│                        │       │                   window paces how quickly they accumulate. A client that
│                        │       │                   keeps the connection
│                        │       │                   open and keeps opening and resetting streams grows server
│                        │       │                   memory without
│                        │       │                   bound. The severity is Low because growth is slow, needs a
│                        │       │                    long-lived
│                        │       │                   connection, and causes no memory corruption or
│                        │       │                   disclosure.
│                        │       │                   FIPS impact: no
│                        │       │                   The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

│                        │       │                   45ca9ce7e60b6 
│                        │       ├ Title           : openssl: openssl: Denial of Service via crafted EC
│                        │       │                   certificate in CMS encryption 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Issue summary: Encrypting a CMS message to an EC
│                        │       │                   certificate whose group order
│                        │       │                   is 1 may cause CMS_encrypt() or CMS_encrypt_ex() to loop
│                        │       │                   indefinitely.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   Impact summary: An attacker able to supply the recipient
│                        │       │                   certificate to an
│                        │       │                   application performing CMS encryption can cause that
│                        │       │                   application to loop
│                        │       │                   indefinitely, consuming CPU and resulting in Denial of
│                        │       │                   Service.
│                        │       │                   CWE: CWE-835: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition
│                        │       │                   ('Infinite Loop')
│                        │       │                   Description: CMS_encrypt() and CMS_encrypt_ex() encrypt a
│                        │       │                   message to one or
│                        │       │                   more recipient certificates and, for an EC recipient,
│                        │       │                   generate an ephemeral
│                        │       │                   key in the recipient's group. If the certificate declares
│                        │       │                   a group order of 1,
│                        │       │                   random scalar generation can only produce zero. The key
│                        │       │                   generation routine
│                        │       │                   then retries without limit while waiting for a nonzero
│                        │       │                   private scalar, so the
│                        │       │                   call never returns.
│                        │       │                   The OpenSSL TLS and QUIC implementations do not use this
│                        │       │                   path. An application
│                        │       │                   is exposed only if it calls CMS_encrypt() or
│                        │       │                   CMS_encrypt_ex() with a recipient
│                        │       │                   certificate whose EC parameters are attacker-controlled.
│                        │       │                   Certificates with
│                        │       │                   normal EC group orders do not trigger the loop.
│                        │       │                   OpenSSL 4.0 and later reject unknown explicit EC groups in
│                        │       │                    default builds.
│                        │       │                   These versions are affected only when configured with the
│                        │       │                   enable-ec_explicit_curves option.
│                        │       │                   The result is a hang that consumes a CPU core until the
│                        │       │                   process is
│                        │       │                   interrupted, a Denial of Service. The severity is Low
│                        │       │                   because the attacker
│                        │       │                   must supply the recipient certificate and the application
│                        │       │                   must choose to
│                        │       │                   encrypt to it; ordinary CMS encryption to trusted
│                        │       │                   recipients is unaffected.
│                        │       │                   The fix makes EC key generation fail when the group has no
│                        │       │                    valid nonzero
│                        │       │                   private scalar, instead of retrying indefinitely.
│                        │       │                   FIPS impact: no
│                        │       │                   The FIPS modules in 4.1, 4.0, 3.5 and 3.0 are not
│                        │       │                   affected. The FIPS provider
│                        │       │                   does not support arbitrary explicit EC domain parameters,
│                        │       │                   so an order-1 group
│                        │       │                   is rejected during key import before the vulnerable key
│                        │       │                   generation path is
│                        │       │                   reached. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       │                   b50e8f272f921 
│                        │       ├ Title           : openssl: openssl: Denial of Service via crafted CMS or
│                        │       │                   PKCS#7 SignedData message 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Issue summary: Verifying a maliciously crafted CMS or
│                        │       │                   PKCS#7 SignedData
│                        │       │                   message with CRL checking enabled may consume excessive
│                        │       │                   CPU time, growing with
│                        │       │                   the square of the message size.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   Impact summary: An attacker who can submit a CMS or PKCS#7
│                        │       │                    SignedData message
│                        │       │                   to an application that verifies it with CRL checking
│                        │       │                   enabled can occupy a CPU
│                        │       │                   core for seconds to minutes, causing Denial of Service.
│                        │       │                   Applications that
│                        │       │                   leave CRL checking disabled are not affected.
│                        │       │                   CWE: CWE-407: Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity
│                        │       │                   Description: With CRL checking enabled, OpenSSL compares
│                        │       │                   each CRL distribution
│                        │       │                   point of a certificate against the issuing distribution
│                        │       │                   point of every
│                        │       │                   candidate CRL. For a nameRelativeToCRLIssuer distribution
│                        │       │                   point, the full name
│                        │       │                   is the CRL issuer name with the relative name appended.
│                        │       │                   Since the change that
│                        │       │                   deferred this computation, crl_crldp_check() rebuilds that
│                        │       │                    full name for each
│                        │       │                   candidate CRL and frees it again.
│                        │       │                   CMS_verify() and PKCS7_verify() take both the distribution
│                        │       │                    points and the
│                        │       │                   candidate CRLs from the message, and this scoring runs
│                        │       │                   before any signature is
│                        │       │                   checked. An application is exposed only if it sets
│                        │       │                   X509_V_FLAG_CRL_CHECK on
│                        │       │                   the store and does not pass CMS_NOCRL or PKCS7_NOCRL; CRL
│                        │       │                   checking is off by
│                        │       │                   default. In TLS the CRLs come from the local store, so a
│                        │       │                   peer controls only
│                        │       │                   the distribution point count.
│                        │       │                   The cost grows with the product of the distribution point
│                        │       │                   count, the CRL count
│                        │       │                   and the issuer name length, all chosen by the message
│                        │       │                   author; a few hundred
│                        │       │                   kilobytes can occupy a CPU core for tens of seconds.
│                        │       │                   Verification still fails
│                        │       │                   as it should, with no crash, no incorrect result and no
│                        │       │                   memory growth.
│                        │       │                   Requiring CRL checking is what limits the severity.
│                        │       │                   FIPS impact: no
│                        │       │                   The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

│                        │       ├ Title           : openssl: openssl: Denial of Service via out-of-bounds read
│                        │       │                    during TLS key-share processing 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Issue summary: A server configured with the Suite B
│                        │       │                   certificate flag through
│                        │       │                   SSL_CTX_set_cert_flags() and with TLS 1.3 enabled may read
│                        │       │                    past the end of a
│                        │       │                   fixed group list when it processes a ClientHello whose
│                        │       │                   supported_groups and
│                        │       │                   key_share contain no Suite B group.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   Impact summary: A remote client can send a ClientHello
│                        │       │                   that makes the server
│                        │       │                   read past the end of a static array. The values read are
│                        │       │                   never returned to the
│                        │       │                   client, so no memory is disclosed; on builds with
│                        │       │                   sanitizers or hardened
│                        │       │                   allocators the read may crash the process, causing Denial
│                        │       │                   of Service.
│                        │       │                   CWE: CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
│                        │       │                   Description: When the Suite B certificate flag is set,
│                        │       │                   OpenSSL restricts the
│                        │       │                   accepted groups to P-256 and P-384 by substituting a fixed
│                        │       │                    two-element list
│                        │       │                   for the configured group list. The tuple machinery used
│                        │       │                   for key-share
│                        │       │                   selection was not updated for this substitution:
│                        │       │                   tls1_get_group_tuples() still
│                        │       │                   returns the configured tuples, which by default describe
│                        │       │                   eight groups. The
│                        │       │                   server-side walk in tls_parse_ctos_key_share() then
│                        │       │                   advances through the
│                        │       │                   two-element list using those tuple counts without checking
│                        │       │                    the cumulative
│                        │       │                   offset against the number of groups present.
│                        │       │                   Only applications that call SSL_CTX_set_cert_flags() with
│                        │       │                   SSL_CERT_FLAG_SUITEB_128_LOS and leave TLS 1.3 enabled are
│                        │       │                    affected. The
│                        │       │                   openssl s_server -suiteB_128 option sets an X.509
│                        │       │                   verification parameter
│                        │       │                   instead, so the stock command line server is not
│                        │       │                   vulnerable. Default
│                        │       │                   configurations do not reach this code.
│                        │       │                   A client that offers only groups outside the Suite B set,
│                        │       │                   such as X25519,
│                        │       │                   forces every tuple to be walked and the read to run past
│                        │       │                   the array. The bytes
│                        │       │                   read are compared against client group IDs and never sent
│                        │       │                   back, so no memory
│                        │       │                   is disclosed. On builds with address sanitizers or
│                        │       │                   hardened allocators the
│                        │       │                   read can abort the process; in ordinary release builds it
│                        │       │                   reads a few bytes of
│                        │       │                   adjacent constant data.
│                        │       │                   FIPS impact: no
│                        │       │                   The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

│                        │       │                   d98f51adf5726 
│                        │       ├ Title           : Issue summary: A QUIC peer that sends many small
│                        │       │                   out-of-order STREAM f ... 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Issue summary: A QUIC peer that sends many small
│                        │       │                   out-of-order STREAM fragments
│                        │       │                   while withholding the first byte of the stream may cause
│                        │       │                   OpenSSL to buffer
│                        │       │                   a large number of reassembly nodes occupying much larger
│                        │       │                   memory than
│                        │       │                   the actual data sent.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   Impact summary: A remote peer can pin large amounts of
│                        │       │                   memory on a server that
│                        │       │                   accepts incoming QUIC streams, potentially exhausting
│                        │       │                   memory and causing
│                        │       │                   Denial of Service.
│                        │       │                   CWE: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or
│                        │       │                   Throttling
│                        │       │                   Description: QUIC receive flow control limits the highest
│                        │       │                   byte offset a peer
│                        │       │                   may reach on a stream. It does not limit how many
│                        │       │                   out-of-order fragments the
│                        │       │                   receiver buffers. OpenSSL allocates a reassembly node for
│                        │       │                   each non-adjacent
│                        │       │                   STREAM fragment and never caps the count. A peer that
│                        │       │                   opens a stream and sends
│                        │       │                   many one-byte fragments at increasing offsets, while
│                        │       │                   withholding the first
│                        │       │                   byte, makes the receiver retain one node per fragment
│                        │       │                   without delivering any
│                        │       │                   data.
│                        │       │                   Only applications that accept incoming streams are
│                        │       │                   exposed. With the default
│                        │       │                   policy, which rejects peer-initiated streams, the stream
│                        │       │                   is torn down before
│                        │       │                   state accumulates. Because the read side never advances
│                        │       │                   past the missing
│                        │       │                   prefix, the flow control window never slides and the nodes
│                        │       │                    stay pinned for the
│                        │       │                   life of the connection.
│                        │       │                   The per-stream window bounds the highest offset, so the
│                        │       │                   memory one stream can
│                        │       │                   pin is finite, but it can reach tens of megabytes and,
│                        │       │                   across many streams and
│                        │       │                   connections, drive memory pressure and Denial of Service.
│                        │       │                   The severity is
│                        │       │                   limited because the exhaustion is bounded by flow control
│                        │       │                   and requires a
│                        │       │                   non-default configuration.
│                        │       │                   FIPS impact: no
│                        │       │                   The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

│                        │       ├ Title           : openssl: OpenSSL: Denial of Service via NULL pointer
│                        │       │                   dereference during DANE TLSA record processing 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Issue summary: A DANE-enabled TLS client may crash by
│                        │       │                   dereferencing a NULL
│                        │       │                   pointer when processing an unusual combination of
│                        │       │                   certificate and TLSA
│                        │       │                   records.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   Impact summary: The impact is limited to a client crash
│                        │       │                   (potential Denial
│                        │       │                   of Service).
│                        │       │                   CWE: CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference
│                        │       │                   Description: A DANE-enabled TLS client that supports TLSA
│                        │       │                   records with at
│                        │       │                   least one of the PKIX-TA(0) or PKIX-EE(1) usages alongside
│                        │       │                    the DANE-TA(2)
│                        │       │                   usage may crash by dereferencing a NULL pointer if the
│                        │       │                   server claims a trusted
│                        │       │                   CA's certificate to be its end-entity certificate and has
│                        │       │                   an unusual mix of
│                        │       │                   associated TLSA records.
│                        │       │                   DANE SMTP clients should not be affected since only the
│                        │       │                   DANE-TA(2) and DANE-EE(3) TLSA record usages are specified
│                        │       │                    applicable
│                        │       │                   in SMTP.  For example, the Postfix MTA is not affected,
│                        │       │                   while the Exim
│                        │       │                   MTA does not at present use OpenSSL's DANE
│                        │       │                   implementation.
│                        │       │                   Use of DANE in validation of RFC7250 raw public keys
│                        │       │                   (RPKs) is also
│                        │       │                   unaffected, as these only use DANE-EE(3) TLSA records.
│                        │       │                   Only applications that support combining the DANE PKI with
│                        │       │                    a traditional PKI
│                        │       │                   are potentially affected.  A DANE-enabled browser or
│                        │       │                   similar, that uses
│                        │       │                   OpenSSL's DANE API could be affected.
│                        │       │                   FIPS impact: no
│                        │       │                   The DANE API is outside the FIPS module boundary.

│                        │       ├ Title           : openssl: openssl: Denial of service via crafted
│                        │       │                   out-of-sequence DTLS handshake fragments 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Issue summary: Receiving crafted out-of-sequence DTLS
│                        │       │                   handshake fragments may
│                        │       │                   cause OpenSSL to allocate a full message-length reassembly
│                        │       │                    buffer for each
│                        │       │                   buffered message, so a small amount of wire data consumes
│                        │       │                   a large amount of
│                        │       │                   memory.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   Impact summary: A remote attacker can send a few small
│                        │       │                   crafted DTLS handshake
│                        │       │                   fragments to make a DTLS server or client allocate well
│                        │       │                   over a megabyte of
│                        │       │                   memory per connection, which may lead to memory exhaustion
│                        │       │                    and Denial of
│                        │       │                   Service if many connections are made.
│                        │       │                   CWE: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or
│                        │       │                   Throttling
│                        │       │                   Description: DTLS handshake messages can arrive out of
│                        │       │                   order and fragmented,
│                        │       │                   so OpenSSL buffers fragments of up to ten out-of-sequence
│                        │       │                   messages until
│                        │       │                   reassembly is possible. When the first fragment of a new
│                        │       │                   message arrives,
│                        │       │                   OpenSSL allocates a buffer sized to the full message
│                        │       │                   length declared in the
│                        │       │                   fragment header, plus a reassembly bitmap, instead of
│                        │       │                   storing only the bytes
│                        │       │                   actually received. The declared length is capped by the
│                        │       │                   maximum certificate
│                        │       │                   list size, 128KB by default, and that cap applies to every
│                        │       │                    handshake message
│                        │       │                   type rather than only to Certificate messages.
│                        │       │                   Only DTLS endpoints reach this code. TLS, QUIC and
│                        │       │                   applications that do not
│                        │       │                   use DTLS are unaffected. An attacker sends fragments that
│                        │       │                   declare a large
│                        │       │                   message length but carry almost no data, using up to ten
│                        │       │                   distinct message
│                        │       │                   sequence numbers.
│                        │       │                   A single connection can then hold roughly 1.4MB of buffers
│                        │       │                    from about 156
│                        │       │                   bytes on the wire. Because the number of buffered messages
│                        │       │                    is capped, memory
│                        │       │                   exhaustion requires many connections or many peers, which
│                        │       │                   is why the severity
│                        │       │                   is Low.
│                        │       │                   FIPS impact: no
│                        │       │                   The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       │                   7fbda4c6b104a 
│                        │       ├ Title           : openssl: openssl: Denial of Service via overlapping QUIC
│                        │       │                   CRYPTO frame processing 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Issue summary: A retransmitted QUIC CRYPTO frame can
│                        │       │                   release packet storage
│                        │       │                   while the TLS record layer retains a direct pointer into
│                        │       │                   that storage causing
│                        │       │                   use after free.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   Impact summary: A malicious QUIC server can cause a
│                        │       │                   heap-use-after-free read
│                        │       │                   in the OpenSSL QUIC client. The server can also identify
│                        │       │                   one allocator-adjacent
│                        │       │                   byte through the client's protected Handshake response.
│                        │       │                   CWE: CWE-416: Use After Free
│                        │       │                   Description: During CRYPTO stream processing, a pointer
│                        │       │                   into the first frame's
│                        │       │                   memory on the stream is lent to the TLS handshake
│                        │       │                   processing. The memory
│                        │       │                   must remain stable until it is processed and released.
│                        │       │                   However the processing
│                        │       │                   of retransmitted CRYPTO frames could release the memory if
│                        │       │                    the retransmitted
│                        │       │                   frame fully overlapped the existing frame. This then
│                        │       │                   causes use-after-free read
│                        │       │                   when the TLS handshake processing continues.
│                        │       │                   The use-after-free read can lead to a Denial-of-Service of
│                        │       │                    the client
│                        │       │                   application or a minor leak of information about the heap
│                        │       │                   memory contents
│                        │       │                   that might be overwritten with other data, subsequently
│                        │       │                   allocated by
│                        │       │                   the application, to the peer.
│                        │       │                   FIPS impact: no
│                        │       │                   The FIPS module is not affected as the QUIC implementation
│                        │       │                    is outside of
│                        │       │                   the OpenSSL FIPS module boundary.

│                        │       ├ Title           : openssl: OpenSSL: Denial of Service via out-of-bounds read
│                        │       │                    in AES-GCM-SIV 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Issue summary: Setting an AES-GCM-SIV IV shorter than the
│                        │       │                   expected nonce
│                        │       │                   length via EVP_CipherInit_ex() may trigger a heap
│                        │       │                   out-of-bounds read.
│                        │       │                   Supplying a longer IV is silently truncated instead of
│                        │       │                   rejected.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   Impact summary: An application passing a caller-supplied
│                        │       │                   IV of the wrong
│                        │       │                   length may crash or read beyond its buffer. Because
│                        │       │                   trailing IV bytes are
│                        │       │                   ignored, an attacker who knows one message and tag may
│                        │       │                   forge messages under a
│                        │       │                   different IV.
│                        │       │                   CWE: CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
│                        │       │                   Description: AES-GCM-SIV copies the caller-supplied IV or
│                        │       │                   nonce into its
│                        │       │                   internal state using a copy whose length is taken from the
│                        │       │                    expected nonce size
│                        │       │                   rather than from the length the caller actually provided.
│                        │       │                   When the caller
│                        │       │                   passes a shorter IV, the copy reads past the end of the
│                        │       │                   caller's buffer;
│                        │       │                   AddressSanitizer confirms a heap out-of-bounds read
│                        │       │                   reached through
│                        │       │                   EVP_CipherInit_ex() into ossl_aes_gcm_siv_init(). When the
│                        │       │                    caller passes a
│                        │       │                   longer IV, the implementation silently discards the
│                        │       │                   trailing bytes instead of
│                        │       │                   rejecting the length.
│                        │       │                   The truncation breaks the binding between the IV and the
│                        │       │                   computed
│                        │       │                   authentication tag. An attacker who has observed a message
│                        │       │                    and its tag under
│                        │       │                   one IV can produce a message and tag that verify under a
│                        │       │                   different IV whose
│                        │       │                   first bytes match, since the surplus bytes never influence
│                        │       │                    the computation.
│                        │       │                   The message itself is unchanged, so this is a failure of
│                        │       │                   IV commitment rather
│                        │       │                   than a classic existential forgery.
│                        │       │                   Only applications that call EVP_CipherInit_ex() (or the
│                        │       │                   equivalent provider
│                        │       │                   cipher initialization) with an IV length other than the
│                        │       │                   standard 12 bytes for
│                        │       │                   AES-GCM-SIV are affected. The severity is limited because
│                        │       │                   the out-of-bounds
│                        │       │                   read is small and attacker-controlled only in length, and
│                        │       │                   the forgery requires
│                        │       │                   an unusual IV length choice by the application.
│                        │       │                   FIPS impact: no
│                        │       │                   The FIPS modules are not affected by this issue, as
│                        │       │                   AES-GCM-SIV is not an
│                        │       │                   approved algorithm. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM
