│                        │       │                   ea3e21d0f52a3 
│                        │       ├ Title           : openssl: openssl: Denial of Service via malformed PEM data
│                        │       │                    in PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Issue summary: When an application passes a stack to
│                        │       │                   PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() to add entries to, and reading
│                        │       │                    fails,
│                        │       │                   OpenSSL frees every entry in the stack, both the old ones
│                        │       │                   and any new
│                        │       │                   ones, but leaves them in the stack.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   Impact summary: An application that passes an existing
│                        │       │                   stack to
│                        │       │                   PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() and keeps using it after a
│                        │       │                   failed read may
│                        │       │                   use memory that was already freed. This can cause a crash
│                        │       │                   or, in
│                        │       │                   principle, memory corruption. Malformed PEM data can make
│                        │       │                   the read fail,
│                        │       │                   but only applications that pass an existing stack are
│                        │       │                   affected, and
│                        │       │                   OpenSSL itself does not do this.
│                        │       │                   CWE: CWE-416: Use After Free
│                        │       │                   Description: PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() reads
│                        │       │                   certificates, CRLs and
│                        │       │                   private keys from PEM data and adds them to a stack of
│                        │       │                   X509_INFO
│                        │       │                   structures. If the application passes a stack that is not
│                        │       │                   NULL, the
│                        │       │                   function adds the new entries to it and must leave the
│                        │       │                   entries that are
│                        │       │                   already there unchanged.
│                        │       │                   If reading fails, the function frees every entry in the
│                        │       │                   stack. This
│                        │       │                   includes the entries that were there before the call, and
│                        │       │                   the entries
│                        │       │                   added by the call. It does not remove these entries from
│                        │       │                   the stack, so
│                        │       │                   the stack keeps pointers to freed memory. The failure can
│                        │       │                   happen at any
│                        │       │                   point, even before any entry was added. A PEM item with
│                        │       │                   invalid content
│                        │       │                   is enough.  This also happens if the stack was empty:
│                        │       │                   entries added
│                        │       │                   before the failure are freed but stay in the stack.
│                        │       │                   An application that then reads or frees the stack will use
│                        │       │                    memory that
│                        │       │                   was already freed. This can crash the application or, in
│                        │       │                   principle,
│                        │       │                   corrupt memory.
│                        │       │                   Only applications that pass a stack that is not NULL are
│                        │       │                   affected.
│                        │       │                   OpenSSL itself never does this. Its own callers, including
│                        │       │                    the code that
│                        │       │                   TLS uses to load CA certificates, always pass NULL. When
│                        │       │                   the stack is
│                        │       │                   NULL, the function frees only the entries that it created
│                        │       │                   itself, which
│                        │       │                   is safe. We expect that very few applications pass an
│                        │       │                   existing stack. An
│                        │       │                   attacker can make the read fail with malformed PEM data,
│                        │       │                   but cannot make
│                        │       │                   an application pass an existing stack.
│                        │       │                   The same problem affects PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio(),
│                        │       │                   PEM_X509_INFO_read()
│                        │       │                   and PEM_X509_INFO_read_ex(), which use the same code.
│                        │       │                   OpenSSL 1.1.1 and
│                        │       │                   1.0.2 have only the first two of these functions.
│                        │       │                   FIPS impact: no
│                        │       │                   The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : LOW

│                        │       │                   881aa86145fec 
│                        │       ├ Title           : openssl: openssl: Out-of-bounds write via integer overflow
│                        │       │                    in EVP_EncodeBlock() 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Issue summary: Calling EVP_EncodeBlock() with an input
│                        │       │                   length close to INT_MAX
│                        │       │                   may overflow the calculation of the encoded output size
│                        │       │                   and write past the end
│                        │       │                   of the caller-supplied output buffer.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   Impact summary: No path by which an attacker can trigger
│                        │       │                   this has been
│                        │       │                   identified. An application that passes an input length
│                        │       │                   near INT_MAX to
│                        │       │                   EVP_EncodeBlock() could suffer a heap buffer overflow,
│                        │       │                   crashing or corrupting
│                        │       │                   its own memory, but it must itself supply such a length.
│                        │       │                   CWE: CWE-190: Integer Overflow or Wraparound
│                        │       │                   Description: EVP_EncodeBlock() base64-encodes a buffer of
│                        │       │                   a caller-supplied
│                        │       │                   length into an output buffer that the caller allocates.
│                        │       │                   The caller is expected
│                        │       │                   to reserve 4*((len+2)/3)+1 bytes. For input lengths close
│                        │       │                   to INT_MAX, the
│                        │       │                   arithmetic that computes the encoded length overflows a
│                        │       │                   signed integer, so the
│                        │       │                   function writes more data than the documented output size.
│                        │       │                    The result is a
│                        │       │                   heap buffer overflow in the calling process.
│                        │       │                   Reaching this requires an application to pass an input
│                        │       │                   length near INT_MAX to
│                        │       │                   EVP_EncodeBlock(). OpenSSL's TLS, QUIC and CMS
│                        │       │                   implementations never encode
│                        │       │                   buffers of that size, and the command line tools cannot
│                        │       │                   practically be made to
│                        │       │                   do so: the limits on reading a proxy password from a file
│                        │       │                   and on bignum sizes
│                        │       │                   prevent it. An application that accepts an
│                        │       │                   attacker-controlled length and
│                        │       │                   forwards it to EVP_EncodeBlock() without its own bound
│                        │       │                   check is exposed.
│                        │       │                   The severity is Low because no attacker-controlled path to
│                        │       │                    the overflow is
│                        │       │                   known. The caller must already hold a buffer of about two
│                        │       │                   gigabytes before the
│                        │       │                   defect can be reached.
│                        │       │                   FIPS impact: no
│                        │       │                   The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : LOW

│                        │       ├ Title           : openssl: openssl: Information disclosure via uninitialized
│                        │       │                    memory in QUIC peer detection 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Issue summary: QUIC, when performing automated peer
│                        │       │                   detection, may allow
│                        │       │                   uninitialized stack data to leak into the received address
│                        │       │                    which is then used
│                        │       │                   as the destination for outgoing packets.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   Impact summary: Applications using QUIC's automated peer
│                        │       │                   detection mechanism
│                        │       │                   may receive an invalid address, leading to connection loss
│                        │       │                    and disclosure of
│                        │       │                   uninitialized stack data to an attacker observing the
│                        │       │                   outgoing network traffic.
│                        │       │                   CWE: CWE-457 (Use of Uninitialized Variable)
│                        │       │                   Description: The OpenSSL QUIC stack contains a feature in
│                        │       │                   which, when using an
│                        │       │                   already connected socket, it will auto-detect the peer
│                        │       │                   address during the SSL
│                        │       │                   handshake.  This feature uses the getpeername() function,
│                        │       │                   passing a buffer of
│                        │       │                   sufficient length to hold any supported address family,
│                        │       │                   but passes a buffer
│                        │       │                   length that is only sized such that larger addresses, such
│                        │       │                    as IPv6, cannot be
│                        │       │                   retrieved. The getpeername() function however, still
│                        │       │                   returns the full address
│                        │       │                   length, which is accepted as the valid input buffer
│                        │       │                   length, leading to the
│                        │       │                   address buffer containing uninitialized stack data instead
│                        │       │                    of the actual peer
│                        │       │                   address. The invalid peer address is then used as
│                        │       │                   destination for the outgoing
│                        │       │                   packets which leads to a connectivity breakage and a
│                        │       │                   leakage of the
│                        │       │                   uninitialized stack data to passive network observers.
│                        │       │                   FIPS impact: no
│                        │       │                   The FIPS modules in 4.0, 3.6, 3.5, 3.4, and 3.0 are not
│                        │       │                   affected by this CVE as
│                        │       │                   the affected protocol is not implemented in the FIPS
│                        │       │                   module. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : LOW

│                        │       │                   68e08c9c22181 
│                        │       ├ Title           : openssl: OpenSSL: Message authentication bypass via
│                        │       │                   zero-length AAD update 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Issue summary: The AES-GCM-SIV implementation treats a
│                        │       │                   zero-length Additional
│                        │       │                   Authenticated Data (AAD) update as a reset of all the AAD
│                        │       │                   supplied so far,
│                        │       │                   instead of leaving the AAD unchanged. An application that
│                        │       │                   supplies its AAD in
│                        │       │                   several fragments, one of which is empty, therefore
│                        │       │                   produces or verifies
│                        │       │                   messages whose authentication tag does not cover the AAD
│                        │       │                   supplied before
│                        │       │                   the empty fragment.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   Impact summary: Data an application intended to
│                        │       │                   authenticate alongside a
│                        │       │                   message is silently left unauthenticated. An attacker can
│                        │       │                   forge the AAD of such
│                        │       │                   a message.
│                        │       │                   CWE: CWE-325: Missing Cryptographic Step
│                        │       │                   Description: An application passing AAD in multiple chunks
│                        │       │                    of which some have
│                        │       │                   zero length will have the previous AAD chunks effectively
│                        │       │                   unauthenticated. Also,
│                        │       │                   on context re-initialisation, the AAD was not reset, which
│                        │       │                    meant that any AAD
│                        │       │                   accumulated from the previous context usage were also
│                        │       │                   included in the AAD of the
│                        │       │                   new message.
│                        │       │                   The fix makes a zero-length AAD update a no-op and clears
│                        │       │                   any accumulated AAD
│                        │       │                   whenever the context is re-initialised with a key or a
│                        │       │                   nonce.
│                        │       │                   A re-initialisation that only changes parameters keeps the
│                        │       │                    AAD.
│                        │       │                   FIPS impact: no
│                        │       │                   The FIPS modules are not affected, as AES-GCM-SIV is not a
│                        │       │                    FIPS approved
│                        │       │                   algorithm and is implemented only in the default provider,
│                        │       │                    outside the
│                        │       │                   OpenSSL FIPS module boundary.

│                        │       ├ Title           : gcc-toolset-15-gcc: gcc: gcc-toolset-16: gcc: Denial of
│                        │       │                   Service via use-after-free in binary heap erase_if 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in GCC. When an application calls the
│                        │       │                   erase_if function on a binary heap priority queue in
│                        │       │                   libstdc++, the library reallocates storage but fails to
│                        │       │                   update its internal entry pointer. An attacker capable of
│                        │       │                   triggering this operation can exploit this use-after-free
│                        │       │                   condition, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) via an
│                        │       │                   application crash or potential memory corruption.

│                        │       │                   search data to an application compiled with parallel mode,

│                        │       │                   Service (DoS).

│                        │       │                   c4d53ecb1c566 
│                        │       ├ Title           : gcc: Integer wrap in `std 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in the libstdc++ component of GCC. An
│                        │       │                   attacker who can provide an excessively large element
│                        │       │                   count to a boolean vector (std::vector<bool>) constructor
│                        │       │                   can trigger an integer wrap during internal memory
│                        │       │                   calculations. This issue leaves the container in an
│                        │       │                   inconsistent state, leading to out-of-bounds memory access
│                        │       │                    and resulting in an application crash or a Denial of
│                        │       │                   Service (DoS) during subsequent operations.

│                        │       ├ Title           : gcc: Stack overflow in std::bitset on libstdc++ 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in GCC libstdc++. When an application
│                        │       │                   extracts data into a bitset from a wide-character stream,
│                        │       │                   internal stack memory allocation fails to properly account
│                        │       │                    for character size and alignment. An attacker capable of
│                        │       │                   supplying crafted input to an affected application could
│                        │       │                   trigger a stack-based buffer overflow leading denial of
│                        │       │                   service (DoS). 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       ├ Title           : libstdc++: overflow leaves streambuf in inconsistent state
│                        │       │                    on I/O error. 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in libstdc++. When a byte-by-byte write
│                        │       │                   operation fails during file stream processing, the library
│                        │       │                    may still append data into the internal memory buffer. An
│                        │       │                    attacker capable of inducing repeated write failures in
│                        │       │                   an affected service can trigger a buffer overflow,
│                        │       │                   potentially resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) or
│                        │       │                   memory corruption.

│                        │       ├ Title           : gcc: Out-of-bounds read in std::from_chars 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in gcc. An attacker could cause a Denial
│                        │       │                   of Service (DoS) by passing a string that is not
│                        │       │                   null-terminated to the std::from_chars() function in the
│                        │       │                   libstdc++ library. This issue triggers an out-of-bounds
│                        │       │                   read beyond the allocated buffer, potentially leading to
│                        │       │                   invalid data parsing or an application crash.

│                        │       ├ Title           : initscripts in rPath Linux 1 sets insecure permissions for
│                        │       │                    the /var/lo ... 
│                        │       ├ Description     : initscripts in rPath Linux 1 sets insecure permissions for
│                        │       │                    the /var/log/btmp file, which allows local users to
│                        │       │                   obtain sensitive information regarding authentication
│                        │       │                   attempts.  NOTE: because sshd detects the insecure
│                        │       │                   permissions and does not log certain events, this also
│                        │       │                   prevents sshd from logging failed authentication attempts
│                        │       │                   by remote attackers.

│                        │       │                   8525a3f50fd9d 
│                        │       ├ Title           : shadow-utils: Default subordinate ID configuration in
│                        │       │                   /etc/login.defs could lead to compromise 
│                        │       ├ Description     : shadow-utils (aka shadow) 4.4 through 4.17.0 establishes a
│                        │       │                    default /etc/subuid behavior (e.g., uid 100000 through
│                        │       │                   165535 for the first user account) that can realistically
│                        │       │                   conflict with the uids of users defined on locally
│                        │       │                   administered networks, potentially leading to account
│                        │       │                   takeover, e.g., by leveraging newuidmap for access to an
│                        │       │                   NFS home directory (or same-host resources in the case of
│                        │       │                   remote logins by these local network users). NOTE: it may
│                        │       │                   also be argued that system administrators should not have
│                        │       │                   assigned uids, within local networks, that are within the
│                        │       │                   range that can occur in /etc/subuid.

│                        │       │                   6.5-20250322 and classified as problematic. This
│                        │       │                   vulnerability affects the function postprocess_termcap of
│                        │       │                   the file tinfo/parse_entry.c. The manipulation leads to
│                        │       │                   stack-based buffer overflow. The attack needs to be
│                        │       │                   approached locally. Upgrading to version 6.5-20250329 is
│                        │       │                   able to address this issue. It is recommended to upgrade
│                        │       │                   the affected component.

│                        │       │                   67e063c5fbaa6 
│                        │       ├ Title           : libtirpc: libtirpc: SunRPC UDP datagram-boundary violation
│                        │       │                    (stale buffer bytes decoded as current request) 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in libtirpc. The SunRPC UDP/datagram
│                        │       │                   server transport reuses a single receive buffer across
│                        │       │                   requests and resets the XDR decode position without
│                        │       │                   rebinding the decode length to the size of the datagram
│                        │       │                   actually received. As a result, when a short UDP RPC
│                        │       │                   request is received after a longer one, the XDR decoder
│                        │       │                   can read stale bytes left in the reused buffer and
│                        │       │                   interpret them as part of the current request, including
│                        │       │                   credential, verifier, or procedure-argument fields. The
│                        │       │                   highest threat from this vulnerability is to data
│                        │       │                   confidentiality and integrity for services that use a
│                        │       │                   UDP-based SunRPC server. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       ├ Title           : libtirpc: libtirpc: Denial of service via unbounded memory
│                        │       │                    allocation during RPCSEC_GSS decoding 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in libtirpc. An authenticated remote
│                        │       │                   attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending
│                        │       │                   oversized wrapped data requests to an RPC (Remote
│                        │       │                   Procedure Call) service configured with RPCSEC_GSS (Remote
│                        │       │                    Procedure Call Security-Generic Security Service)
│                        │       │                   integrity or privacy. This can lead to unbounded memory
│                        │       │                   allocation, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) by
│                        │       │                   exhausting system resources and causing the service to
│                        │       │                   become unstable or terminate.

│                        │       ├ Title           : libtirpc: libtirpc: Denial of Service via unbounded memory
│                        │       │                    allocation during portmapper response decoding 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in libtirpc. A remote attacker can
│                        │       │                   exploit this vulnerability by sending specially crafted
│                        │       │                   PMAPPROC_DUMP replies to a client application that uses
│                        │       │                   the pmap_getmaps() function against an attacker-controlled
│                        │       │                    host. This unbounded decoding can lead to excessive
│                        │       │                   memory and CPU allocation, causing the client process to
│                        │       │                   experience a Denial of Service (DoS) due to resource
│                        │       │                   exhaustion.

│                        │       │                   e557e83cdc808 
│                        │       ├ Title           : libtirpc: libtirpc: SunRPC UDP datagram-boundary violation
│                        │       │                    (stale buffer bytes decoded as current request) 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in libtirpc. The SunRPC UDP/datagram
│                        │       │                   server transport reuses a single receive buffer across
│                        │       │                   requests and resets the XDR decode position without
│                        │       │                   rebinding the decode length to the size of the datagram
│                        │       │                   actually received. As a result, when a short UDP RPC
│                        │       │                   request is received after a longer one, the XDR decoder
│                        │       │                   can read stale bytes left in the reused buffer and
│                        │       │                   interpret them as part of the current request, including
│                        │       │                   credential, verifier, or procedure-argument fields. The
│                        │       │                   highest threat from this vulnerability is to data
│                        │       │                   confidentiality and integrity for services that use a
│                        │       │                   UDP-based SunRPC server. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: failed external mount helper still
│                        │       │                    runs privileged X-mount post-hooks 
│                        │       ├ Description     : util-linux versions through 2.41.5 and 2.42.2 fail to
│                        │       │                   check mount helper exit status before running post-mount
│                        │       │                   hooks, allowing unprivileged users to execute privileged
│                        │       │                   operations on pre-existing filesystems. Attackers can
│                        │       │                   exploit X-mount.idmap or X-mount.owner hooks to clone
│                        │       │                   filesystems with inherited suid bits or modify target
│                        │       │                   inode permissions after a helper fails, achieving
│                        │       │                   privilege escalation.

│                        │       │                   1aab83503caae 
│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: nsenter --join-cgroup leaks root
│                        │       │                   cgroup migration authority 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The nsenter --join-cgroup option opens the target
│                        │       │                   cgroup.procs file as root and leaves that file descriptor
│                        │       │                   open across later namespace and credential changes and
│                        │       │                   across execve(). Because the kernel checks later cgroup
│                        │       │                   migrations using the credentials from the original open, a
│                        │       │                    program run in an attacker-controlled target can inherit
│                        │       │                   root's ability to move host processes between cgroups.
│                        │       │                   After a privileged operator uses --join-cgroup against
│                        │       │                   that target, an unprivileged user can migrate and
│                        │       │                   terminate unrelated root processes.

│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: X-mount.subdir detached-tree
│                        │       │                   resolution can escape via intermediate symlinks 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The X-mount.subdir option uses a detached-tree fast path
│                        │       │                   on Linux 6.15 and later and passes the configured
│                        │       │                   subdirectory to open_tree() with AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW. That
│                        │       │                    flag does not stop intermediate symlink traversal or keep
│                        │       │                    resolution inside the newly mounted filesystem. A local
│                        │       │                   unprivileged user with an fstab-authorized X-mount.subdir
│                        │       │                   entry can attach a host path at the intended mountpoint.[

│                        │       │                   bccb51ae263a2 
│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: restricted bind mounts do not pin
│                        │       │                   the source, allowing X-mount.owner/group/mode
│                        │       │                   redirection 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in util-linux. Restricted bind mounts
│                        │       │                   take the source path from fstab but do not pin that source
│                        │       │                    before the privileged mount. A local unprivileged user
│                        │       │                   who can replace the authorized source or a writable
│                        │       │                   ancestor can redirect SUID mount(8) to bind another host
│                        │       │                   directory. If the fstab entry also sets X-mount.owner,
│                        │       │                   X-mount.group, or X-mount.mode, root then changes
│                        │       │                   ownership or mode on that redirected inode.

│                        │       │                   baf7ac76c48e1 
│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: Access control bypass due to
│                        │       │                   improper hostname canonicalization 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in util-linux. Improper hostname
│                        │       │                   canonicalization in the `login(1)` utility, when invoked
│                        │       │                   with the `-h` option, can modify the supplied remote
│                        │       │                   hostname before setting `PAM_RHOST`. A remote attacker
│                        │       │                   could exploit this by providing a specially crafted
│                        │       │                   hostname, potentially bypassing host-based Pluggable
│                        │       │                   Authentication Modules (PAM) access control rules that
│                        │       │                   rely on fully qualified domain names. This could lead to
│                        │       │                   unauthorized access.

│                        │       │                   193ff182c80f9 
│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: partial disclosure of arbitrary files in chfn
│                        │       │                   and chsh when compiled with libreadline 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in the util-linux chfn and chsh utilities
│                        │       │                    when compiled with Readline support. The Readline library
│                        │       │                    uses an "INPUTRC" environment variable to get a path to
│                        │       │                   the library config file. When the library cannot parse the
│                        │       │                    specified file, it prints an error message containing
│                        │       │                   data from the file. This flaw allows an unprivileged user
│                        │       │                   to read root-owned files, potentially leading to privilege
│                        │       │                    escalation. This flaw affects util-linux versions prior
│                        │       │                   to 2.37.4.

│                        │       ├ Title           : libxml2: double-free/UAF in libxml2 Python bindings 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in libxml2 with Python bindings enabled.
│                        │       │                   A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by
│                        │       │                   providing a specially crafted XML document containing a
│                        │       │                   Document Type Definition (DTD) with enumerated attribute
│                        │       │                   values. This triggers a double-free error in the SAX
│                        │       │                   attributeDecl callback handler, where a string is freed
│                        │       │                   twice. This flaw can lead to a denial of service (DoS) due
│                        │       │                    to a reproducible crash in Python applications using the
│                        │       │                   libxml2 SAX bindings. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : HIGH

│                        │       │                   73afc8a4fef64 
│                        │       ├ Title           : libxml2: libxml2: Data integrity issues due to integer
│                        │       │                   overflow in write callbacks 
│                        │       ├ Description     : In xmlIO in libxml2 before 2.15.4, an inconsistency in
│                        │       │                   xmlOutputWriteCallback and xmlBufUse causes negative
│                        │       │                   lengths to reach write callbacks, aka a lack of a check
│                        │       │                   for integer overflow before calling writecallback. This
│                        │       │                   has security relevance for many types of uses of that
│                        │       │                   length value within a callback.

│                        │       ├ Title           : libxml2: libxml2: Information disclosure, SSRF, or denial
│                        │       │                   of service due to improper parseFlags propagation. 
│                        │       ├ Description     : In xinclude in libxml2 before 2.15.4, xmlXIncludeProcess
│                        │       │                   and xmlXIncludeProcessTree do not propagate parseFlags.
│                        │       │                   This has security relevance for, for example, the
│                        │       │                   XML_PARSE_NONET flag, if (without it) a custom resource
│                        │       │                   loader accesses the internet and triggers XML external
│                        │       │                   entity injection, SSRF, or a denial of service (e.g., for
│                        │       │                   an attacker-controlled internet resource that is
│                        │       │                   intentionally slow).

│                        │       ├ Title           : libxml2: libxml2: NULL pointer dereference parsing
│                        │       │                   nextCatalog without catalog attribute 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in libxml2. A local user or an attacker
│                        │       │                   providing a specially crafted XML catalog can trigger a
│                        │       │                   NULL pointer dereference during XML catalog parsing. This
│                        │       │                   occurs when a `nextCatalog` element lacks its mandatory
│                        │       │                   `catalog` attribute, leading to the application crashing
│                        │       │                   and causing a Denial of Service (DoS).

│                        │       │                   2d63dcb46f377 
│                        │       ├ Title           : libxml2: libxml2: Arbitrary code execution in xmlcatalog
│                        │       │                   utility via buffer overflow 
│                        │       ├ Description     : libxml2 is vulnerable to multiple stack-based buffer
│                        │       │                   overflows in the xmlcatalog utility when running in
│                        │       │                   --shell mode. The usershell() function processes user
│                        │       │                   input using fixed-size stack buffers without proper bounds
│                        │       │                    checking.
│                        │       │                   By supplying an overly long input line, an attacker can
│                        │       │                   overflow internal buffers (command, arg, and argv) during
│                        │       │                   input parsing. This results in memory corruption within
│                        │       │                   the stack frame.
│                        │       │                   Successful exploitation may cause a crash or potentially
│                        │       │                   allow arbitrary code execution in the context of the
│                        │       │                   xmlcatalog process.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   This issue has been fixed in the commit c2e233fc.
│                        │       │                   NOTE:
│                        │       │                   The maintainers of this project did not agree that this
│                        │       │                   issue is a vulnerability and considered it a bug.

│                        │       │                   use-after-free vulnerability in xmlValidatePopElement

│                        │       │                   validation states. Attackers supplying an XML document
│                        │       │                   ending inside an element to an application reusing a
│                        │       │                   DTD-validating xmlTextReader can trigger heap reads,
│                        │       │                   causing crashes and limited heap disclosure via error
│                        │       │                   messages.

│                        │       ├ Description     : libxml2 through 2.15.4 contains a heap use-after-free
│                        │       │                   vulnerability that allows attackers to crash applications
│                        │       │                   by triggering xmlFreeNode on a stale reader->faketext node
│                        │       │                    after xmlTextReader reuse. Attackers can supply XML
│                        │       │                   containing a namespace declaration to applications that
│                        │       │                   read its value and reuse the reader, causing a freed
│                        │       │                   document's dictionary read and process crash.

│                        │       │                   reader->state when a reader is reused. Attackers can
│                        │       │                   submit one malformed XML document to an application
│                        │       │                   reusing a single reader, causing every later document to
│                        │       │                   be rejected until the reader is recreated.

│                        │       │                   reader->input again after xmlTextReaderClose() already

│                        │       │                   with xmlReaderNewWalker() can crash, and groomed heap
│                        │       │                   memory can control the close callback for possible code
│                        │       │                   execution.

│                        │       ├ Description     : GNOME libxml2 2.12.6 through 2.15.4 contains a NULL
│                        │       │                   pointer dereference vulnerability in
│                        │       │                   xmlTextReaderConstEncoding() after a reader is reset with
│                        │       │                   xmlReaderNewWalker(). Because xmlCtxtReset() leaves
│                        │       │                   ctxt->input NULL, querying the document encoding makes
│                        │       │                   xmlGetActualEncoding() read ctxt->input->flags without a
│                        │       │                   check, crashing the application and causing denial of
│                        │       │                   service.

│                        │       ├ Description     : GNOME libxml2 2.14.0 through 2.15.4 contains a missing NUL
│                        │       │                    termination flaw in xmlBufferAddHead() in buf.c that
│                        │       │                   leaves uninitialized heap bytes as the terminator for
│                        │       │                   storage-less buffers. Attackers supplying data to
│                        │       │                   applications reusing an xmlBuffer can trigger over-reads
│                        │       │                   via xmlBufferCat() and xmlStrlen(), disclosing adjacent
│                        │       │                   heap memory or causing crashes.

│                        │       │                   of service.

│                        │       │                   b5b114efbdaae 
│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: glibc: Memory corruption via out-of-bounds write in
│                        │       │                    wide scanf functions 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Calling the wide scanf family of functions (swscanf,
│                        │       │                   fwscanf, wscanf, vswscanf, vfwscanf and vwscanf) with a %s
│                        │       │                    or %[ conversion without the 'l' length modifier in the
│                        │       │                   GNU C Library version 2.2 to version 2.44 writes an extra
│                        │       │                   null byte one past the end of the destination array when
│                        │       │                   the converted multibyte string and its terminating null
│                        │       │                   byte exactly fill that array.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   These conversions store each wide input character into the
│                        │       │                    caller's char array as a multibyte sequence.  The
│                        │       │                   conversion ends with the sequence that returns to the
│                        │       │                   initial shift state, which also stores the terminating
│                        │       │                   null byte, and the functions then append a second null
│                        │       │                   byte.  A destination sized for the converted string and
│                        │       │                   one terminator, as the C standard requires the caller to
│                        │       │                   provide, is therefore written one byte past its end.  The
│                        │       │                   out-of-bounds byte is always a null byte, which may
│                        │       │                   corrupt adjacent data or crash the process.  An attacker
│                        │       │                   who supplies the input can trigger the overflow with a
│                        │       │                   string whose converted length exactly fills the
│                        │       │                   destination.
│                        │       │                   The narrow scanf functions, the %ls and %l[ conversions
│                        │       │                   into a wchar_t array, and the 'a' and 'm' allocation
│                        │       │                   modifiers are not affected, and storing a wide scanf
│                        │       │                   conversion into a narrow char array is uncommon.  This
│                        │       │                   issue affects all architectures and ABIs supported by the
│                        │       │                   GNU C Library.

│                        │       │                   12a48d78582c7 
│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: glibc: Denial of Service via out-of-bounds read in
│                        │       │                   CP949 character conversion 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Converting crafted CP949 input to UTF-8 character encoding
│                        │       │                    and ignoring invalid characters, in the GNU C Library
│                        │       │                   version 2.1 or later may result in the converter reading
│                        │       │                   past the end of the input buffer, causing the calling
│                        │       │                   application to crash.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   When the CP949 decoder encounters an invalid input byte
│                        │       │                   sequence like '\xa2\xe8' it ends up advancing the pointer
│                        │       │                   tracking the read buffer position twice.  If //IGNORE is
│                        │       │                   set on the destination encoding and this sequence is at
│                        │       │                   the end of the input buffer, the decoder may then end up
│                        │       │                   reading past the bounds of the input buffer.  To exploit
│                        │       │                   this, the target iconv function needs to set //IGNORE on
│                        │       │                   the destination of the conversion and the input and
│                        │       │                   encoding needs to be attacker controlled.

│                        │       │                   d0d58f99c7da1 
│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: glibc: Arbitrary code execution via directory
│                        │       │                   traversal in LANGUAGE environment variable 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The gettext family of functions in the GNU C Library
│                        │       │                   version 2.0 and later accept LANGUAGE environment variable
│                        │       │                    entries that contain '/' or that are equal to "..",
│                        │       │                   unless the program is setuid or setgid (AT_SECURE).  An
│                        │       │                   attacker who can set LANGUAGE in the environment of a
│                        │       │                   program that uses gettext can make it load a message
│                        │       │                   catalog (.mo file) from an arbitrary location in the file
│                        │       │                   system.  A crafted .mo file can crash the program through
│                        │       │                   out-of-range offsets, or supply translations whose format
│                        │       │                   directives do not match the arguments passed by the
│                        │       │                   program.  That causes undefined behaviour in the printf
│                        │       │                   family of functions and may allow arbitrary code execution
│                        │       │                    with the privileges of the program.  The safety of
│                        │       │                   message catalogs relies on them being installed in
│                        │       │                   trusted, read-only locations, and the directory traversal
│                        │       │                   bypasses this.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   The fix for CVE-2014-0475 rejects ".." path components in
│                        │       │                   locale names passed to setlocale or taken from the LC_ALL,
│                        │       │                    LC_* and LANG environment variables.  gettext reads
│                        │       │                   LANGUAGE directly and appends each colon-separated entry
│                        │       │                   to the message catalog directory, so that fix did not
│                        │       │                   cover LANGUAGE.
│                        │       │                   LANGUAGE is only used when the LC_MESSAGES locale is not
│                        │       │                   "C", "C.<encoding>" or "POSIX", so the attacker must also
│                        │       │                   be able to select another installed locale, for example
│                        │       │                   through LANG or LC_ALL.  Exploitation also requires that
│                        │       │                   the attacker can place the crafted file in a location
│                        │       │                   readable by the target program, and that the environment
│                        │       │                   crosses a trust boundary without the program running as
│                        │       │                   AT_SECURE.  An example is an SSH server that accepts
│                        │       │                   LANGUAGE and LANG from clients through the AcceptEnv
│                        │       │                   directive and restricts an account to a forced command;
│                        │       │                   the attacker may use this to escape the restriction.

│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: glob implementation can cause excessive CPU and
│                        │       │                   memory consumption due to crafted glob expressions 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The glob implementation in the GNU C Library (aka glibc or
│                        │       │                    libc6) allows remote authenticated users to cause a
│                        │       │                   denial of service (CPU and memory consumption) via crafted
│                        │       │                    glob expressions that do not match any pathnames, as
│                        │       │                   demonstrated by glob expressions in STAT commands to an
│                        │       │                   FTP daemon, a different vulnerability than
│                        │       │                   CVE-2010-2632.

│                        │       │                   26c2e5c0bdc04 
│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: glibc: Denial of Service via memory allocation
│                        │       │                   failure during regular expression processing 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The regcomp and regexec functions in the GNU C Library
│                        │       │                   version 2.3 to version 2.44 may read freed memory and free
│                        │       │                    the same heap block twice when a memory allocation fails
│                        │       │                   while a regular expression is compiled or matched.  The
│                        │       │                   re_dfa_add_node (the NFA node table) and build_range_exp
│                        │       │                   (bracket ranges) grow several arrays with consecutive
│                        │       │                   realloc calls and store the new pointers only after all of
│                        │       │                    them succeed.  When a later call fails, the pattern
│                        │       │                   buffer keeps pointers to blocks that were already freed,
│                        │       │                   and the error cleanup frees them again.  In regexec, the
│                        │       │                   back-reference cache (match_ctx_add_entry) frees its array
│                        │       │                    when a realloc fails but keeps the pointer, which is
│                        │       │                   freed again on the error path.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   An attacker does not need to supply a crafted regular
│                        │       │                   expression: patterns large enough to grow these arrays are
│                        │       │                    common.  The failure has to hit a specific allocation,
│                        │       │                   though, so the issue can only be reached when the system
│                        │       │                   is already under memory pressure.  An attacker who
│                        │       │                   supplies the pattern or the subject string has little
│                        │       │                   control over which allocation fails, so the expected
│                        │       │                   impact is a crash of the process.  This issue affects all
│                        │       │                   architectures and ABIs supported by the GNU C Library.

│                        │       │                   49409db5cd997 
│                        │       ├ Title           : glibc: glibc: Denial of Service via double free in glob
│                        │       │                   functions 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The glob functions in the GNU C Library versions 2.44 and
│                        │       │                   earlier may free the same heap block twice when a memory
│                        │       │                   allocation fails while glob prepends the directory name to
│                        │       │                    the names it matched.  The names already rewritten are
│                        │       │                   freed, but their pointers stay in the result vector, and
│                        │       │                   the error path frees them again with globfree.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   The allocation must fail after at least one name has been
│                        │       │                   rewritten, so the issue can only be reached when the
│                        │       │                   process is already close to its memory limit, for example
│                        │       │                   under an address space limit (RLIMIT_AS) or on a 32-bit
│                        │       │                   system.  The attacker needs control to make the result
│                        │       │                   large enough to make the program or service run out of
│                        │       │                   memory, either by controlling the glob pattern and having
│                        │       │                   knowledge of the filesystem layout or through other means.
│                        │       │                     This issue affects all architectures and ABIs supported
│                        │       │                   by the GNU C Library.

│                        │       ├ Title           : Converting crafted ISO-2022-CN-EXT input in the GNU C
│                        │       │                   Library version  ... 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Converting crafted ISO-2022-CN-EXT input in the GNU C
│                        │       │                   Library version 2.2 through 2.44 may result in the
│                        │       │                   converter reading past the end of the input buffer,
│                        │       │                   causing the calling application to crash.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   When the ISO-2022-CN-EXT decoder encounters an invalid
│                        │       │                   input byte sequence like '\x0e' it ends up advancing the
│                        │       │                   pointer tracking the read buffer position twice.  If this
│                        │       │                   sequence is at the end of the input buffer, the decoder
│                        │       │                   may then end up reading past the bounds of the input
│                        │       │                   buffer.  To exploit this, the input and encoding needs to
│                        │       │                   be attacker controlled.

│                        │       │                   0c29bfaf20751 
│                        │       ├ Title           : Converting crafted input from UCS-4 to IBM1390 or IBM1399
│                        │       │                   character en ... 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Converting crafted input from UCS-4 to IBM1390 or IBM1399
│                        │       │                   character encoding, in the GNU C Library version 2.3.3 and
│                        │       │                    later may result in the converter reading past the end of
│                        │       │                    the input buffer, causing the calling application to
│                        │       │                   crash.
│                        │       │                   
│                        │       │                   When converting from UCS-4, these encoders may encounter a
│                        │       │                    combining base such as U+00E6 and jump ahead by 4 bytes
│                        │       │                   to check the next UCS-4 code point.  The check for end of
│                        │       │                   buffer however does not account for this, which may result
│                        │       │                    in a buffer overread if the following code point has less
│                        │       │                    than 4 bytes remaining.  Exploitation of this bug not
│                        │       │                   only requires attacker control of input and encoding, but
│                        │       │                   also strict control over layout of the input in memory.

│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: failed external mount helper still
│                        │       │                    runs privileged X-mount post-hooks 
│                        │       ├ Description     : util-linux versions through 2.41.5 and 2.42.2 fail to
│                        │       │                   check mount helper exit status before running post-mount
│                        │       │                   hooks, allowing unprivileged users to execute privileged
│                        │       │                   operations on pre-existing filesystems. Attackers can
│                        │       │                   exploit X-mount.idmap or X-mount.owner hooks to clone
│                        │       │                   filesystems with inherited suid bits or modify target
│                        │       │                   inode permissions after a helper fails, achieving
│                        │       │                   privilege escalation.

│                        │       │                   ee6edc9352ddf 
│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: nsenter --join-cgroup leaks root
│                        │       │                   cgroup migration authority 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The nsenter --join-cgroup option opens the target
│                        │       │                   cgroup.procs file as root and leaves that file descriptor
│                        │       │                   open across later namespace and credential changes and
│                        │       │                   across execve(). Because the kernel checks later cgroup
│                        │       │                   migrations using the credentials from the original open, a
│                        │       │                    program run in an attacker-controlled target can inherit
│                        │       │                   root's ability to move host processes between cgroups.
│                        │       │                   After a privileged operator uses --join-cgroup against
│                        │       │                   that target, an unprivileged user can migrate and
│                        │       │                   terminate unrelated root processes.

│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: X-mount.subdir detached-tree
│                        │       │                   resolution can escape via intermediate symlinks 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The X-mount.subdir option uses a detached-tree fast path
│                        │       │                   on Linux 6.15 and later and passes the configured
│                        │       │                   subdirectory to open_tree() with AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW. That
│                        │       │                    flag does not stop intermediate symlink traversal or keep
│                        │       │                    resolution inside the newly mounted filesystem. A local
│                        │       │                   unprivileged user with an fstab-authorized X-mount.subdir
│                        │       │                   entry can attach a host path at the intended mountpoint.[

│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: restricted bind mounts do not pin
│                        │       │                   the source, allowing X-mount.owner/group/mode
│                        │       │                   redirection 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in util-linux. Restricted bind mounts
│                        │       │                   take the source path from fstab but do not pin that source
│                        │       │                    before the privileged mount. A local unprivileged user
│                        │       │                   who can replace the authorized source or a writable
│                        │       │                   ancestor can redirect SUID mount(8) to bind another host
│                        │       │                   directory. If the fstab entry also sets X-mount.owner,
│                        │       │                   X-mount.group, or X-mount.mode, root then changes
│                        │       │                   ownership or mode on that redirected inode.

│                        │       │                   334d144898951 
│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: Access control bypass due to
│                        │       │                   improper hostname canonicalization 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in util-linux. Improper hostname
│                        │       │                   canonicalization in the `login(1)` utility, when invoked
│                        │       │                   with the `-h` option, can modify the supplied remote
│                        │       │                   hostname before setting `PAM_RHOST`. A remote attacker
│                        │       │                   could exploit this by providing a specially crafted
│                        │       │                   hostname, potentially bypassing host-based Pluggable
│                        │       │                   Authentication Modules (PAM) access control rules that
│                        │       │                   rely on fully qualified domain names. This could lead to
│                        │       │                   unauthorized access.

│                        │       │                   db7f08cf0cc9d 
│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: partial disclosure of arbitrary files in chfn
│                        │       │                   and chsh when compiled with libreadline 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in the util-linux chfn and chsh utilities
│                        │       │                    when compiled with Readline support. The Readline library
│                        │       │                    uses an "INPUTRC" environment variable to get a path to
│                        │       │                   the library config file. When the library cannot parse the
│                        │       │                    specified file, it prints an error message containing
│                        │       │                   data from the file. This flaw allows an unprivileged user
│                        │       │                   to read root-owned files, potentially leading to privilege
│                        │       │                    escalation. This flaw affects util-linux versions prior
│                        │       │                   to 2.37.4.

│                        │       ├ Title           : initscripts in rPath Linux 1 sets insecure permissions for
│                        │       │                    the /var/lo ... 
│                        │       ├ Description     : initscripts in rPath Linux 1 sets insecure permissions for
│                        │       │                    the /var/log/btmp file, which allows local users to
│                        │       │                   obtain sensitive information regarding authentication
│                        │       │                   attempts.  NOTE: because sshd detects the insecure
│                        │       │                   permissions and does not log certain events, this also

│                        │       │                   045ea6ca71535 
│                        │       ├ Title           : shadow-utils: Default subordinate ID configuration in
│                        │       │                   /etc/login.defs could lead to compromise 
│                        │       ├ Description     : shadow-utils (aka shadow) 4.4 through 4.17.0 establishes a
│                        │       │                    default /etc/subuid behavior (e.g., uid 100000 through
│                        │       │                   165535 for the first user account) that can realistically
│                        │       │                   conflict with the uids of users defined on locally
│                        │       │                   administered networks, potentially leading to account
│                        │       │                   takeover, e.g., by leveraging newuidmap for access to an
│                        │       │                   NFS home directory (or same-host resources in the case of
│                        │       │                   remote logins by these local network users). NOTE: it may
│                        │       │                   also be argued that system administrators should not have
│                        │       │                   assigned uids, within local networks, that are within the
│                        │       │                   range that can occur in /etc/subuid.

│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: failed external mount helper still
│                        │       │                    runs privileged X-mount post-hooks 
│                        │       ├ Description     : util-linux versions through 2.41.5 and 2.42.2 fail to
│                        │       │                   check mount helper exit status before running post-mount
│                        │       │                   hooks, allowing unprivileged users to execute privileged
│                        │       │                   operations on pre-existing filesystems. Attackers can
│                        │       │                   exploit X-mount.idmap or X-mount.owner hooks to clone
│                        │       │                   filesystems with inherited suid bits or modify target
│                        │       │                   inode permissions after a helper fails, achieving
│                        │       │                   privilege escalation.

│                        │       │                   67082c4433745 
│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: nsenter --join-cgroup leaks root
│                        │       │                   cgroup migration authority 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The nsenter --join-cgroup option opens the target
│                        │       │                   cgroup.procs file as root and leaves that file descriptor
│                        │       │                   open across later namespace and credential changes and
│                        │       │                   across execve(). Because the kernel checks later cgroup
│                        │       │                   migrations using the credentials from the original open, a
│                        │       │                    program run in an attacker-controlled target can inherit
│                        │       │                   root's ability to move host processes between cgroups.
│                        │       │                   After a privileged operator uses --join-cgroup against
│                        │       │                   that target, an unprivileged user can migrate and
│                        │       │                   terminate unrelated root processes.

│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: X-mount.subdir detached-tree
│                        │       │                   resolution can escape via intermediate symlinks 
│                        │       ├ Description     : The X-mount.subdir option uses a detached-tree fast path
│                        │       │                   on Linux 6.15 and later and passes the configured
│                        │       │                   subdirectory to open_tree() with AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW. That
│                        │       │                    flag does not stop intermediate symlink traversal or keep
│                        │       │                    resolution inside the newly mounted filesystem. A local
│                        │       │                   unprivileged user with an fstab-authorized X-mount.subdir
│                        │       │                   entry can attach a host path at the intended mountpoint.[

│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: restricted bind mounts do not pin
│                        │       │                   the source, allowing X-mount.owner/group/mode
│                        │       │                   redirection 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in util-linux. Restricted bind mounts
│                        │       │                   take the source path from fstab but do not pin that source
│                        │       │                    before the privileged mount. A local unprivileged user
│                        │       │                   who can replace the authorized source or a writable
│                        │       │                   ancestor can redirect SUID mount(8) to bind another host
│                        │       │                   directory. If the fstab entry also sets X-mount.owner,
│                        │       │                   X-mount.group, or X-mount.mode, root then changes
│                        │       │                   ownership or mode on that redirected inode.

│                        │       │                   96455087b64e1 
│                        │       ├ Title           : util-linux: util-linux: Access control bypass due to
│                        │       │                   improper hostname canonicalization 
│                        │       ├ Description     : A flaw was found in util-linux. Improper hostname
│                        │       │                   canonicalization in the `login(1)` utility, when invoked
│                        │       │                   with the `-h` option, can modify the supplied remote
│                        │       │                   hostname before setting `PAM_RHOST`. A remote attacker
│                        │       │                   could exploit this by providing a specially crafted
│                        │       │                   hostname, potentially bypassing host-based Pluggable
│                        │       │                   Authentication Modules (PAM) access control rules that
│                        │       │                   rely on fully qualified domain names. This could lead to
│                        │       │                   unauthorized access.
